Title: Tree falls on 2 cars in Pasir Belanda, no injuries reported
Article:
BAYAN LEPAS: A falling tree damaged two cars in Pasir Belanda here this morning. No injuries were reported.
Bayan Lepas assemblyman Datuk Azrul Mahathir Aziz said the incident occurred in the morning and the fallen tree blocked part of the road.
"No casualties were reported. We thank the Fire and Rescue Department and the Kampung Terang fire and rescue team for coming to assist," he said in a Facebook post.
He also thanked the Penang Island City Council's Engineering Department for inspecting the area and clearing tree branches obstructing traffic on the road to Gertak Sanggul.
"Although it was not part of their duties, they still came forward to help."
This comes a day after three people, including a 9-year-old girl, were injured when a
30m-tall Angsana tree
fell on a Perodua Ativa in Jalan Macalister.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rantau Panjang residents pray for Aliff ahead of title fight
Article:
RANTAU PANJANG: Residents and supporters here have pledged to perform regular solat hajat (special prayers) for local Muay Thai fighter Ahmad Nor Iman Aliff Rakib as he prepares for the biggest fight of his career.
The champion, better known as Aliff Rakib, made history last month when he knocked out Thai legend Sam-A Gaiyanghadao in the fifth round at Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok to capture the ONE interim strawweight Muay Thai World Championship.
The victory made Aliff the first Malaysian fighter to win a Muay Thai world championship belt in ONE Championship.
He is now targeting a title unification bout against undisputed strawweight Muay Thai world champion Prajanchai PK Saenchai in October.
Support for Aliff was evident when residents and fans gathered for a solat hajat ceremony for the fighter at his new house in Taman Sri Rantau Mas here today.
Retired soldier Mohamad Faizal Che Ibrahim, 43, who has known Aliff for more than 10 years, said the victory was a source of pride for the people of Rantau Panjang.
"I am very proud to see a son of Rantau Panjang win and bring home a world championship belt.
"I hope he wins his next fight and continues to make us proud. We will continue to support him and pray for his success.
"We have agreed to perform solat hajat regularly to pray for his safety and success," he said.
Self-employed Azmi Mustafa, 56, said he was happy to see supporters turning up to celebrate Aliff's achievement and offer encouragement ahead of his next challenge.
"I am happy to see people coming to celebrate Aliff today and give him encouragement.
"It is not often that a son of Rantau Panjang becomes a world champion. His achievement is something we can all be proud of.
"He is not only a source of pride for Rantau Panjang, but for the whole of Malaysia," he said.
The community's prayers and support are expected to continue as Aliff prepares for the potential unification bout, which could see him become the undisputed ONE strawweight Muay Thai world champion.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid: Rauf given full mandate to negotiate Melaka election cooperation
Article:
GERIK: Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has been given full authority to negotiate cooperation with any political coalition ahead of the upcoming Melaka state election.
Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi expressed hoped that the negotiations would not become complicated.
"Discussions about seat allocations are usually complicated. Discuss them properly, there is no problem that cannot be resolved," he told a press conference after officiating the launch of the 2026-2035 National Social Determinants of Health Strategic Plan for Orang Asli (NSPSDHOA) at Kampung Air Banun here today.
Zahid, who is also Umno president, said the decisions reached during the discussions would be conveyed to Umno's top leadership before being brought to the BN Supreme Council for final approval.
Yesterday, Pakatan Harapan communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said it welcomed BN's openness regarding the distribution of seats for the upcoming Melaka state election and described it as an opportunity that deserves to be examined.
Meanwhile, Perikatan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar said that it was also open and ready to hold discussions with BN for the Melaka state polls.
On Saturday, Ahmad Zahid said the coalition remains open to negotiations on seat allocations for the Melaka state election, including seat swaps, provided they are conducted honestly and in good faith.

Title: Pakistan PM wishes Anwar speedy recovery after procedure
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif today wished Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim a speedy recovery following a medical procedure the Malaysian leader had undergone.
"Wishing my dear brother, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, a swift and smooth recovery during his medical procedures.
"May Allah SWT bless him with a speedy return to his duties," he said in a post on X today.
Shehbaz said the people of Pakistan had joined him in praying for Anwar's continued good health and well-being.
Anwar completed an elective laparoscopic procedure to treat an abdominal hernia.
Datuk Dr Asri Rangga Abdullah Ramaiah, head of the prime minister's medical team, said the procedure was carried out smoothly under the care of a team of medical specialists.
"The prime minister has successfully undergone an elective laparoscopic surgical procedure to treat a para-umbilical hernia.
"He is currently undergoing physiotherapy and remains under the supervision of the medical specialist team to ensure a smooth recovery," Dr Asri Rangga said in a statement shared on Anwar's social media accounts.
Earlier today, Anwar's senior press secretary, Tunku Nashrul Abaidah, said the prime minister was undergoing
medical examinations
and would remain under observation for two days.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bursa Malaysia ends marginally lower as investors stay on sidelines
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ended marginally lower on Monday, as investors largely stayed on the sidelines and adopted a wait-and-see approach amid uncertainties over US monetary policy and geopolitical developments, an analyst said.
At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) eased 0.38 of a point to 1,735.37 compared with last Friday's close of 1,735.75.
The index opened 0.10 of a point higher at 1,735.85 and fluctuated between 1,730.35 and 1,738.97 throughout the day.
However, on the broader market, gainers thumped losers 707 to 447, while 573 counters were unchanged, 1,046 untraded and 21 suspended.
Turnover narrowed to 3.49 billion units valued at RM2.55 billion from 3.55 billion units valued at RM3.47 billion last Friday.

Title: Court upholds RM169.22mil asset freeze against businessman Ricky Wong and others
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Court of Appeal today upheld a High Court order to freeze assets worth up to RM169.22 million belonging to businessman Datuk Ricky Wong Shee Kai, his mother Teh Sew Wan and their company, Wong SK Holdings Sdn Bhd.
The freeze was granted in a civil suit filed by the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) over alleged market misconduct.
A three-member panel, chaired by Federal Court judge Datuk Ravinthran N. Paramaguru and comprising Court of Appeal judges Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing and Datuk Leonard David Shim, delivered a unanimous decision.
The panel ruled that the High Court judge had correctly applied the relevant legal principles and properly exercised his discretion.
Shim, who delivered the court's decision via Zoom, said the panel found that the High Court had the authority to grant interim and inter partes injunctions under Section 360 of the Capital Markets and Services Act 2007 (CMSA).
The provision allows the court to restrain the appellants from disposing of or dealing with their assets while the case is pending.
"It is our unanimous decision that Order 29 Rules of Court 2012 and the common law principles of Mareva injunction do not apply to an application for a statutory injunction under Section 360 of the CMSA.
"We therefore find that there was a prima facie case that the appellants have jointly and severally contravened Section 179 of the CMSA and made unlawful pecuniary gains of at least RM56 million from the fraud.
"Thus, it is desirable for the court to grant the interim injunction under Section 360(2) of the CMSA," the judge said.
Shim also said the court found, in any event, that there was a good arguable case and a real risk of dissipation of assets.
He pointed out that more than RM3.5 million from the proceeds had been used to purchase a high-end property at Four Seasons Place, supporting the finding of a genuine risk that the assets might be disposed of or removed from the jurisdiction.
"It is undisputed that Madam Teh (Teh Sew Wan) co-signed 71 cheques and payment vouchers payable to the various nominee companies, and the proceeds of the corporate exercise flowed into the bank accounts of Ricky Wong and Wong SK Holdings.
"The circumstances in which the alleged fraudulent scheme was perpetrated against BPI, involving the layering of corporate entities, fake invoicing, transfer of proceeds from BPI to the various nominee companies controlled by Ricky Wong, and eventually into the bank accounts of Ricky Wong and Wong SK Holdings, show that there is a prima facie case of breach of Section 179 of the CMSA, and it is reasonably likely that the appellants may dispose of the assets," he said.
The panel also dismissed the appellants' contention that the SC had failed to disclose the revocation of earlier freezing and seizure orders, finding that the information had been fully disclosed in the SC's affidavit and written submissions, while the revocation order itself had been exhibited before the High Court.
"Based on the aforesaid reasons, it is our unanimous decision that the learned High Court judge exercised his discretion based on correct principles, and appellate interference is not warranted.
"Hence, the decision of the High Court is affirmed, and the appeals herein are dismissed with costs," said the judge.
The court ordered the appellants to pay RM50,000 in costs for each of the four appeals, totalling RM200,000.
The main trial in the matter is ongoing before the High Court.
Lawyers Tan Sri Cecil Abraham, Alex Tan and Chin Jia Yi appeared for Teh, while Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah and Muhammad Farhan Muhammad Shafee appeared for Wong and Wong SK Holdings.
The SC was represented by Datuk Lim Chee Wee, Kwan Will Sen, Ng Kar Man, Esther Hong and Manveer Singh.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Former Thai MP detained after shooting Nonthaburi local govt official
Article:
BANGKOK: A former Thai lawmaker was detained after allegedly shooting the president of the Nonthaburi Provincial Administrative Organisation (PAO) and injuring his driver at the PAO office in Nonthaburi province, northwest of Bangkok, on Monday.
Nonthaburi Governor Chettha Mosikarat said the incident occurred at 11am when the suspect allegedly opened fire on PAO president Police Colonel Thongchai Yenprasert and his driver.
He said both victims suffered serious injuries and were taken to hospital for treatment.
"I know both parties, the alleged perpetrator and the injured person. They were friends in the past and had a good relationship.
"However, it is believed that their discussion did not reach an agreement, which led to the incident. For the details, we have to wait until police complete their questioning to establish the actual motive," he told reporters on Monday.
Royal Thai Police identified the suspect as former Nonthaburi member of parliament Chalong Riawraeng, who surrendered to police and was taken to Rattanathibet Police Station for questioning.
Provincial Police Region 1 commissioner Police Lieutenant General Wattana Yichin led the investigation at the police station, according to police.
The incident came just two days after a 14-year-old student of Debsirin Nonthaburi School allegedly shot his grandparents dead before opening fire at the school, killing eight people, including teachers and students.
The suspect was later found dead at the school with a gunshot wound to the head.
Twenty-one others were injured in the rampage and taken to hospital for treatment, with eight reported to be in critical condition.

Title: [UPDATED] Wong Chen resigns as Subang MP
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Wong Chen today confirmed his resignation as the Subang member of Parliament.
In a Facebook post today, Wong said he had handed his resignation letter to Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul when they met on Aug 5.
The resignation takes effect at 5pm today.
Wong said he and Johari had agreed to withhold details of the resignation until the effective date and time.
"The delay was to give parliamentary officers three working days to prepare for the vacancy of the Subang parliamentary seat," he said in a statement.
He said he would hold a press conference about 11am on Wednesday to elaborate on his resignation.
"I will also drop the honorific title 'Yang Berhormat' from all my correspondence starting next month," he said.
Speculation over Wong's political future had been building since his Aug 5 meeting with Johari.
Johari had previously been quoted as saying that
Wong had voiced his intention to resign
and explained his reasons, although the Speaker did not confirm at the time whether a formal resignation letter had been handed over.
Wong Chen, a three-term MP first elected in 2013, has represented Subang for PKR since 2018. He was previously the non-executive chairman of Malaysia Debt Ventures Bhd, a position from which he was removed in May.
His resignation comes months after former economy minister Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli and Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad resigned from PKR and vacated their parliamentary seats in May to lead Parti Bersama Malaysia.
Wong was among several PKR members present at the launch of the new party.
In May, Wong
alleged that his office had been denied access
to the MyKhas Portal without prior notice.
He was also among
five PKR lawmakers
who criticised the party's decision to block Ampang MP Rodziah Ismail's access to the MyKhas special allocation portal.
Unity government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, in response, had said that  MyKhas constituency allocations were
intended to benefit the people
and were not funds that MPs could use.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gold edges higher as Fed hike bets fade, US inflation data in focus
Article:
NEW YORK: Gold inched higher on Monday after prices hit a seven-week high in the previous session, as weak US jobs data tempered expectations for Federal Reserve rate hikes and investors look ahead to inflation data for fresh clues on the central bank's policy path.
Spot gold was up 0.1 per cent at US$4,345.09 per ounce, as of 0856 GMT. Prices hit their highest since June 17 on Friday after weak US nonfarm payrolls data.
US gold futures rose 0.1 per cent to US$4,404.80 on Monday.
"Gold prices continue to benefit from last week's positive momentum, following the disappointing US jobs report and the resulting reduction in expectations of further Fed rate hikes," said ActivTrades senior analyst Ricardo Evangelista.
Data showed the US economy unexpectedly shed jobs in July, while previously reported job gains for the prior two months were revised sharply lower, weakening expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike next month.
Traders are now pricing a 44 per cent chance of a rate hike in September, compared to 57 per cent before the jobs report, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.
A lower interest rate environment boosts the attractiveness of gold against income-generating assets, as bullion earns no interest.
Investors are now awaiting US consumer price data due on Wednesday and producer price data on Thursday for further clues on the Fed's interest-rate outlook.
Economists polled by Reuters expect the July consumer price index to have risen 3.4 per cent year-on-year, compared with 3.5 per cent in June.
"A headline figure below the consensus forecast of 3.4 per cent could further reduce expectations of a Fed rate increase before the end of the year, weakening the dollar and creating upside potential for gold," said Evangelista.
On the geopolitical front, Iran said it was nearing a final pact with Oman defining new shipping lanes between them through the Strait of Hormuz, but reiterated that the US must meet several conditions before the strategic waterway is reopened.
Spot silver rose 0.9 per cent to US$64.14 per ounce, while platinum fell 0.4 per cent to US$1,737.42, and palladium lost 1.2 per cent to US$1,360.75.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iran says Saudi-Pakistan-Turkiye deal shows 'change in perception' towards US
Article:
TEHERAN: Iran's foreign ministry said Monday that a defence pact signed last week between Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan was "a sign of a change in the perception" of countries in the region towards the United States.
"The countries of the region have realised that security is not a commodity that can be bought from false brokers," said ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei at a weekly press conference, referring to the US, an ally of the three signatories to the pact.
"Countries in the region cannot rely on the claim of security provided by the US as in the past," he added.
He also said Iran was not concerned that the pact could be aimed at Teheran, highlighting "deep religious, historical and civilisational ties" with Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan.
There was "no reason to worry that this treaty will be against Iran", Baqaei said.
The three nations signed the agreement on Friday against the backdrop of a five-month war between the US and Iran, which has drawn in surrounding nations and disrupted regional shipping routes.
Pakistan's foreign ministry said Friday that the pact meant an attack on any member would be regarded as an attack on all, adding it was "intended to strengthen collective deterrence."
Analysts have said it seeks to deter an emboldened Iran and offset an unreliable United States.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kind-hearted stranger helps visually impaired man see again
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: As Malaysia prepares to celebrate its 69th National Day, the meaning of independence takes on a deeply personal significance for 65-year-old Mohd Din Deli: the freedom to see, move independently and, most importantly, live with dignity.
For four years, darkness had been Din's reality as advanced cataracts in both eyes left him visually impaired and forced him to give up his job as a security guard at a private company here, leaving him dependent on the kindness of strangers on the streets of Kuala Lumpur.
"This walking stick became my eyes because I could no longer see where I was going," he said.
With no means of supporting himself, Din, who is divorced and has lost contact with his two children, rented a small room at a budget hotel near Puduraya, now known as Pudu Sentral, here for RM30 a day and spent his days seeking help from members of the public.
"I would begin my day about 5.30am and stay on the streets until evening. Some people gave me food, while others offered small amounts of money. Some days, I would not even receive a single sen," he said, holding back tears.
His circumstances changed when a businessman who frequently passed by his usual spot near Kortumalai Pillaiyar Temple here noticed his plight.
The businessman, Datuk Seri Jeyenderan Ramasamy, would stop to help Mohd Din cross the road and sometimes give him money for his daily needs.
"I recognised him only by his voice because I could not see his face. It was only later that I learned he was the owner of a shipping company. His acts of kindness meant so much to me," said Din.
He said he had earlier gone for an eye examination, hoping there was still a chance to regain his sight. However, his hopes were dashed when he was told that cataract surgery would cost RM1,800, an amount he could not afford.
"I felt helpless and believed I would spend the rest of my life living in darkness," he said, adding that when he told Jeyenderan about his condition, the businessman immediately arranged for Din to undergo further medical examinations and cataract surgery.
"On Aug 4, I finally opened my eyes after the successful procedures, and now I see the world I thought I would never see again," he said.
Consultant ophthalmologist Dr Manjit Singh of Manjit Singh Eye Specialist Centre here confirmed that Din's vision had deteriorated severely but could be restored through cataract surgery.
"His cataracts were already severely advanced when he first came to us. After successful surgery on both eyes, his vision has now returned to normal," said the eye specialist.
Din, meanwhile, said after the surgery, Jeyenderan offered him a job as a security guard at his company, giving him the opportunity to return to work and rebuild his life.
"I was shocked to receive the job offer and overwhelmed with gratitude. He gave me back something I thought I had lost forever... my sight. Now, he has also given me a chance to rebuild my life. I will always be thankful for his compassion and sincere help during the darkest period of my life.
"This year, I will be able to see the National Day fireworks with my own eyes. Being able to see them would be a true 'Merdeka' for me," he said joyfully.
Jeyenderan said he was moved by Din's plight and decided to lend him a helping hand.
The businessman said he also felt sad that Din had to depend on others to hold his hand and accompany him to the mosque for Friday prayers.
"Today, he can walk to the mosque on his own and perform his prayers," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AfD on pre-election roll in east Germany, despite economists' scepticism
Article:
LARS Gottschligg bought an abandoned building in the east German state of Saxony-Anhalt, covered it with solar panels and transformed it into a sleek black cube that harvests and stores energy, houses data centres and charges electric cars.
"We turned a lost place into a place for the future," the boss of SSC Hydrovent explained during a tour of his plant in the town of Quedlinburg.
Yet with regional elections looming, Gottschligg is unconcerned by the rise of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), which wants, among other things, a greater role for conventional energy sources and less support for renewables.
The AfD is polling at around 41 per cent in Saxony-Anhalt, which votes on Sept 6, and 36 per cent in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, voting on Sept 20.
While in western Germany much AfD support stems from opposition to immigration, experts say that in eastern Germany, the issue matters less.
More significant is the states' shared east German legacy of shrinking populations, shortages of skilled labour, and higher unemployment and lower incomes than in western Germany.
Studies suggest the AfD's rise is fuelled by a lingering sense of economic disadvantage, 36 years after east and west Germany united, and of neglect by a political establishment still largely rooted in the west.
"The people I talk to — and I feel this way myself too — we're not afraid of it," Gottschligg said. "(The AfD) are going to bring about a great deal of change – in fact, they're already doing so."
Both states are among the hardest hit by the shrinking of east Germany's workforce, particularly the young.
The population of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, with its ports and sandy beaches on the Baltic, has fallen by nearly a fifth since reunification.
Saxony-Anhalt has the highest share of pension-age people in Germany: 52 for every 100 of working age.
"Labour is the scarcest production factor in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern's future," said Oliver Holtemoeller from the Halle Institute for Economic Research (IWH).
Unsurprisingly, GDP per capita there is only around 76 per cent of the national average, and labour productivity around 86 per cent, he said.
[[nid:1508215]]
A study by the economic research institute DIW Berlin shows that, where younger, well-educated people are leaving and over-60s are more numerous, the AfD scores significantly higher.
Pablo Himmelspach, 29, comes from near Demmin, a small town in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern with "a lot of older people, and a lot of people who left", but decided to stay.
Studying at Rostock University, and singing as half of the rap duo Hinterlandgang or "Back-country Gang", he says optimism is in fact growing among the young who remain, who for a long time lacked places and opportunities to express themselves:
"I get the feeling that in my generation it's no longer such a big thing that everyone wants to move away."
Hinterlandgang's latest song, "Mitlaeufer" ("Followers"), reflects their mood and that of younger residents who worry about the rise of extremism: "The AfD is 'mainstream', but we're not just following the crowd."
Peter Holdt has taken matters into his own hands. After seeing through his teenage daughter how little there was for teenagers to do in the city of Wismar, he created a travelling "Disco Bus."
Fitted with oversized speakers and disco lights, it brings DJs to villages and schoolyards: "I get in the bus, drive somewhere and make kids happy."
Wismar's mayor, Frank Junge, said the bus fills a gap that the municipal budget, more straitened than in the west, cannot cover.
Guido Friebel, project leader at the Rockwool Foundation Berlin and professor at Goethe University in Frankfurt, said that "many people in eastern Germany still feel their concerns are not being heard by politicians."
However, economists say the AfD's policies would be particularly negative for the economically less developed east.
"Although much of the dissatisfaction among people in strong AfD regions is understandable, they would harm themselves the most by voting for the AfD," said Marcel Fratzscher, president of DIW Berlin.
A study by his institute says this is because, in areas that disproportionately back the AfD, businesses are generally smaller than in the west, workers have lower qualifications, and economic options are more limited.
Under AfD policies — including withdrawal from the euro and the European Union, a halt to immigration, and cuts in state spending — Saxony-Anhalt would lose an average €1,600 (US$1,840) a head in annual income and 10,000 jobs, DIW estimated.
[[nid:1508214]]
Hans-Thomas Tillschneider, AfD deputy chair in Saxony-Anhalt, disagreed, saying:
"If the AfD were able to implement its measures, such as ending all CO2 levies and lifting sanctions against Russia, the result would be a dramatic reduction in the cost of all forms of energy, a sharp rise in foreign trade and, consequently, a massive economic boom."
The marine engineering programme at the University of Rostock — a port and former shipbuilding centre that is often associated with deprivation and far-right agitation — suggests a different route to success.
It had only 10 students per year until the course was internationalised and redesigned with input from local companies, said programme director Sascha Kosleck.
Annual enrolment rose to about 200 within two semesters, drawing students from India, Pakistan, Egypt and beyond.
"We naturally hope that many of them will also stay here in the region and enrich the (labour) market," Kosleck said.
The prospect of an AfD victory worries him - particularly its proposals to charge non-EU students tuition fees.
Gottschligg, with his renewable-energy projects, might also be hamstrung by AfD policies, in his case on high-carbon fossil fuels. But he says he has nothing to fear.
"People want a healthy environment, and they want affordable energy," Gottschligg said.
"If renewable energy makes economic sense, then I don't think even an AfD government would stand in its way."
* The writer is from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police review CCTV footage to track man who set woman on fire
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police are reviewing closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage from around Taman Pusat Kepong to identify and track down a man who allegedly set a 62-year-old woman on fire yesterday.
Sentul acting district police chief Superintendent Jasni Zolpa said investigators were examining footage from the surrounding area to establish the suspect's movements before and after the attack.
"We have collected CCTV footage and are in the process of reviewing it.
"The identity of the suspect and motive for the attack are still subject to further investigation," he said when contacted today.
Jasni said the victim was in critical but stable condition and was receiving treatment at Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL).
In the 8am incident, the woman, who worked as a counter attendant at the outlet, suffered burns to
about 50 per cent of her body
after an unidentified man allegedly doused her with a liquid believed to be petrol before setting her alight.
Police had earlier said the victim was in critical but stable condition.
Initial investigations found that she had no known enemies and had not received any threats before the attack.
The Kuala Lumpur police forensic team also collected DNA samples and other items from the scene to assist investigations.
Police have launched a special operation to track down the suspect. The case is being investigated under Section 326 of the Penal Code.
It was also reported that Kepong member of parliament
Lim Lip Eng
is offering a RM5,000 reward for information leading to the arrest of the suspect.
He said information on the incident at Taman Pusat Kepong must be credible and directly lead to the suspect's arrest.
Those with information on the incident are urged to contact investigating officer Inspector Muhammad Amri Firdaus Jusoh at 010-9198209 or any nearby police station.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Miti continues to strengthen E&E sector to ensure Malaysia remains global technology supply player
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) will continue to empower the electrical and electronics (E&E) sector to ensure Malaysia remains an important player in the global technology supply chain.
Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin said the E&E sector is one of the important fields contributing to Malaysia's position in the global supply chain, including high-tech semiconductors, advanced sensors, and telecommunications.
"This step is important given that Malaysia, especially Penang and the Northern Region, is among the major hubs for the E&E industry, semiconductors, high-tech sensors, and telecommunications. More importantly, the region hosts hundreds of world-class technology manufacturers.
"The E&E sector, particularly the semiconductor industry, plays a strategic role in the country's economy, with Malaysia being one of the important locations in the global value chain, including semiconductor assembly, testing, and packaging activities," he told reporters after officiating the 2010 Strategic Trade Act (STA) Customer Day and the STA Northern Region Clinic programme in Bayan Lepas today.
Sim, who is also the Member of Parliament for Bayan Baru, said Miti is also paying attention to export control compliance aspects to ensure the country's technology sector and international trade operate in an orderly manner.
Meanwhile, he said Malaysia's strong trade performance in the first six months of the year provides local companies with an opportunity to improve the welfare of workers, which is among the main contributors to their success.
Therefore, Sim hopes that companies that achieved good performance can share their success with employees through salary increases and bonuses.
Regarding the Northern Region STA Clinic, he said the programme, attended by 86 participants, serves as Miti's annual engagement platform with industry players, allowing them to receive direct advisory services related to product classification, permit applications, dealings with licensing agencies, and internal audits.
Sim noted that close collaboration between the government and industry players is crucial to ensure Malaysia remains a trusted destination for investment and the production of high-impact technology.

Title: PH-BN talks could be political gimmick ahead of Melaka polls - Takiyuddin
Article:
KOTA BARU: Perikatan Nasional believes Pakatan Harapan's claim that it will negotiate with Barisan Nasional could merely be a political gimmick or strategy ahead of the Melaka election.
PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said no assumptions could be made at this stage as the coalition had yet to receive any confirmation on the alleged talks.
"Regarding whether there have been negotiations between PH and BN in Melaka, I have no information about that.
"As far as we are concerned, we are still holding discussions with BN. I do not know about discussions between PH and BN," he told reporters here last night.
Takiyuddin, who is also Pas secretary-general, said even if negotiations between PH and BN were taking place, it would be premature to draw any conclusions as the matter had yet to be verified.
"If it is true that there are negotiations between PH and BN, we still cannot make any assumptions because the matter has not been confirmed.
"It should be asked of Umno whether it is true or whether there are indeed negotiations between PH and BN," he said.
On PN's negotiations with Umno for the state election, Takiyuddin said such discussions did not necessarily require formal letters to be exchanged, as meetings and negotiations could be held directly.
"In the context of negotiations with Umno for the election, previously we did not necessarily send an official letter. Instead, we held meetings and negotiations.
"On the Pas side, it has been decided that we are still allowed and have been asked to hold negotiations with Umno on the issue of seat allocation," he said.
He said Pas had its own negotiation committee, while PN also had a negotiation mechanism involving all component parties.
"So far, Pas is still holding negotiations with Umno and we have no information about any informal negotiations involving other parties," he said.
PKR information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil yesterday said the party
is in discussions with all
parties
ahead of the Melaka election, including BN.
He said Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh had expressed openness to cross-party engagement, which PKR welcomed.
He added Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Rauf has expressed openness to discussing with any party and PKR welcomed this, adding that Melaka PKR acting chairman Adam Adli Abdul Halim had held several preliminary discussions.
Fahmi also welcomed BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's statement that the coalition was ready to discuss seat arrangements for Melaka and at federal level ahead of the next general election.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Banking veteran Azlan Hashim dies at 85
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prominent banker Datuk Azlan Hashim, who spent more than three decades helping shape the AmBank group, has died at the age of 85.
Azlan was a long-serving board member of AMMB Holdings Bhd (AmBank) and served as its deputy chairman until his retirement in 2015.
He was the younger brother to AmBank founder and former chairman Tan Sri Azman Hashim.
AmBank paid tribute to its former leader in an Instagram post, saying his contributions formed an important part of the group's history.
"His dedicated service, wise leadership and invaluable contributions to the group's governance, growth and development will always be remembered by the AmBank family," it said.
Azlan's association with AmBank began in 1982 when he joined the board of Arab Malaysian Development Bank Bhd, now known as AmInvestment Bank Bhd.
He was appointed chairman of AmSecurities Sdn Bhd in 1986, a position he held until 2007, before joining the board of AMMB Holdings in 1992.
Over more than three decades with the group, Azlan held leadership positions across several subsidiaries and related entities.
He served as a director of Arab Malaysian Eagle Assurance Bhd, now known as AmMetLife Insurance Bhd, from 1985 to 2006, including as chairman and deputy chairman.
He also served on the boards of AmBank Islamic and AmREIT Managers Sdn Bhd, and was a member of the board of trustees of AmGroup Foundation from its incorporation in 1985.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nga: Big data system to guide housing development next year
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Housing and Local Government Ministry will introduce a big data analytics system next year to help developers determine the types, prices and locations of homes needed before launching projects.
Its minister, Nga Kor Ming, said the initiative aimed to address the persistent mismatch between property supply and actual market demand, which was a key factor contributing to the country's property overhang.
The system will consolidate data from federal, state and local authorities, including information on regional income levels and housing needs.
"The main problem in our housing sector is not supply and construction, but a mismatch where the products being offered are not what is needed.
"This is why we have overhang properties," he told reporters after launching the National Housing Policy 2026-2035 today.
While the system will not be mandatory, he said developers could subscribe to the platform to improve the feasibility of their projects.
"They are smart; they know they will not build what the market doesn't want," he said.
The system is also expected to eventually incorporate artificial intelligence (AI) to identify suitable housing products and price points for specific areas.
He said a data-driven approach would allow for a more
nuanced
definition of "affordable housing", moving away from a blanket RM300,000 benchmark that does not account for regional differences in income and property values.
"Imagine the price of an affordable home in Kuala Krai, Kelantan, being the same as Bukit Bintang, Kuala Lumpur. It is not scientific.
"We need big data so developers can build according to a definition that better reflects reality," he said.
Furthermore, the ministry intends to use the data to regulate development approvals in areas already facing significant oversupply.
"If Zone A is already massively oversupplied, then we can pull the brake slightly and slow down," Nga said.
Under the National Housing Policy 2026-2035, the ministry aims to deliver one million affordable homes by 2035 based on actual demand, leveraging technologies such as AI, big data and industrialised building systems.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Greece battles new fire near Athens driven by winds
Article:
ATHENS: A new wildfire broke out in Greece Monday morning southeast of the capital Athens, fanned by strong winds of more than 70 kilometres per hour, firefighters said.
At least 172 firefighters and around 40 vehicles have been deployed to fight the blaze in Kouvaras, 60 km southeast of Athens, in the Attica region, the fire service announced on X.
"Two water-bombing aircraft and four helicopters" are also taking part, the service added.
Agios Stylianos, a village near Kouvaras, has been ordered to evacuate by civil protection authorities.
It marks the second fire near Athens this summer, after one that broke out 10 days ago northwest of the Greek capital and destroyed more than 11,000 hectares of pine forests and farmland.
Because of gusts reaching up to 130 km/h, it took five days to bring the fire under control.
Two helicopter crew members died in a collision with another helicopter while battling the flames.
Like much of the Mediterranean, Greece has experienced increasingly frequent and intense wildfires that scientists link to climate change.
The country remains on extreme alert and several regions are still classified at a very high fire risk.
Experts have warned about the increased severity of the fires affecting Attica, where Athens is located.
From 2017 to 2026, 42 per cent of the total forest area in the region burned because of 15 major fires.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: DKU seeks to intervene in four Undangs' bid to remove Tuanku Muhriz
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Negri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) and its secretary Raja Norazli Raja Nordin have applied to intervene in a legal bid by three former Undangs and a serving one to compel the state menteri besar to sign a proclamation removing Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as ruler.
The intervention application was filed yesterday through Messrs Halim & Ismail, ahead of the four Undangs' leave application to initiate the hearing before High Court judge Norliza Othman here today.
The four — Datuk Mubarak Thahak, Datuk Maarof Mat Rashid, Datuk Abd Rahim Yasin and Datuk Muhammed Abdullah — filed the judicial review in July, naming the menteri besar and the state government as respondents.
They are seeking a court order compelling the menteri besar to recognise Tuanku Muhriz's removal and the validity of the proclamation recognising Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Jaafar as his successor under the state Constitution.
According to court documents sighted by the NST, the DKU and Raja Norazli claimed they had a direct interest in the judicial review and would be directly affected by any orders made by the court.
Federal senior counsel Nurhafizza Azizan said the High Court had advised the applicants to discuss and decide whether to continue the case here or transfer it to Seremban.
Speaking to reporters after today's proceedings, Nurhafizza said judge Norliza Othman conveyed the matter during the hearing of the leave application for judicial review in her chambers.
It was reported that the judicial review application is supported by an affidavit affirmed by Muhammed.
According to his affidavit, the four attended a DKU meeting chaired by Tuanku Muhriz on March 5, during which Mubarak allegedly raised several purported violations of adat.
Muhammed claimed the meeting became heated before the four left and gathered at Balai Undang Sungai Ujong, where they discussed the alleged offences and concluded that Tuanku Muhriz was no longer qualified to remain Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
He claimed representatives from the state government, including the state legal adviser, were also present at the second meeting.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Industronics faces up to US$5.15mil exposure in lawsuit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Loss-making Industronics Bhd could face a bill of up to US$5.15 million (RM21.06 million) after being sued by Bluemount Investment Fund SPC over matters arising from a loan agreement.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Industronics said the dispute stems from a loan agreement dated March 24, 2025 and also involves allegations relating to certain directors and officers.
The amount comprises the principal sum and accrued interest as at April 2, 2026, excluding further interest and legal costs. No liability has been determined by the court at this stage.
Industronics said the writ was not accompanied by a statement of claim, and the company is still assessing the full basis and particulars of the suit with its legal advisers.
"The final financial impact, if any, will depend on the outcome of the suit and any further pleadings or orders of the court," it said.
The lawsuit is not expected to have any material impact on the group's day-to-day business operations at this stage.
The company has appointed legal counsel to advise on and defend the suit and said it would take the necessary steps to protect its interests.
Industronics is currently classified as a Practice Note 17 company and is in the midst of formulating a regularisation plan to address its financial condition.
In its latest monthly update on Aug 3, the company said it had about nine months to submit the regularisation plan to the relevant authorities for approval.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Retired teacher ordered to pay RM88k for slapping student four times seven years ago
Article:
KOTA BARU: A retired teacher was ordered by the High Court here today to pay RM88,069 in total damages to a student whom he slapped four times during a lesson seven years ago.
High Court judge Datuk Mohd Rosli Yusoff made the ruling after allowing a civil suit filed by the victim, through his mother, against the teacher and three other defendants.
The victim, Mohamad Adam Maidin, 21, and his mother, Noor Azleen Mohamad, 47, filed the suit against the teacher, Isamuddin Ismail, 63, who was also the school's senior assistant for administration, naming him as the first defendant.
In his ruling, Mohd Rosli said the teacher had committed a battery against the victim by slapping his face and both cheeks with his right and left hands from behind.
"The teacher, as an educator, also had a duty of care towards the student," he said.
Adam was a Form Two student aged 14 when the incident occurred at about 10am on Jan 28, 2019.
During the incident, the victim was allegedly at his desk with his classmates when the teacher approached him from behind and slapped him four times.
As a result, the victim experienced pain in his face and both ears, as well as dizziness, reduced hearing and ringing in his ears.
His mother then took him to Berek 12 Health Clinic before he was referred to Universiti Sains Malaysia Hospital in Kubang Kerian for an examination by an ear specialist.
A medical report issued in June 2019 found that the victim had hearing problems in his right ear, including mild to moderate mixed hearing loss, which was diagnosed as a traumatic injury believed to have been caused by the slapping.
Following the incident, the victim suffered trauma and was forced to transfer to another school about a month later as he was afraid to return to school and face the teacher.
Meanwhile, counsel for the plaintiffs, Mohd Syukran Mohd Noordin, said the court had allowed his clients' claim against all the defendants after finding negligence and a duty of care in relation to the incident.
"The RM88,069 awarded by the court comprises RM45,000 in general damages, RM569 in special damages, RM11,250 in exemplary damages and RM11,250 in aggravated damages, in addition to RM20,000 in interest and costs," he said.
The civil suit was filed through Messrs Syukran Noordin in March 2021, about two years after the incident.
In the suit, the victim also named the school's principal, the Education director-general and the Malaysian Government as defendants.
The defendants were represented by Senior Federal Counsel Siti Syakimah Ibrahim.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penang cancels 29,240 automated parking compounds
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Penang has cancelled 29,240 parking compounds issued using the Automated Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) system for parking outside designated bays.
State Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H'ng Mooi Lye said the decision was made after the state government took note of public concerns over the system's inability to determine whether a vehicle was parked illegally or had briefly stopped to pick up or drop off passengers.
He said the compounds, issued by the Penang Island City Council (MBPP) in 2025 and up to August this year, would be cancelled, while motorists who had paid could apply for refunds until Sept 30.
"Implementation to use ANPR to issue summonses is halted. All summonses will be issued manually.
"Penang has cancelled 29,240 parking compounds issued through the ANPR system for parking outside designated bays. Of the total, the Penang Island City Council (MBPP) has managed to collect RM266,160 in compounds," he said at a press conference today.
H'ng said enforcement against vehicles parked outside designated bays would now be carried out manually by enforcement officers from the local authorities, based on the actual conditions at the location.
However, enforcement would continue against vehicles parked in no-parking areas or those causing obstruction.
He said motorists who had received compounds for failing to pay parking charges could also appeal for cancellation if they had made payment within 10 minutes of the compound being issued.
Refunds for compounds paid through the Penang Smart Parking application would be credited automatically to users' wallets.
Those who had paid through kiosks or other channels would have to submit the required documents to the respective local authorities to process their claims.
H'ng said the state government had ordered the suspension and review of ANPR for issuing automated compounds following a meeting with MBPP mayor Datuk Ir A. Rajendran and his team on Aug 7.
He stressed that the decision did not mean ANPR technology itself had been scrapped.
"ANPR is actually a system to help us read number plates. We will not use ANPR to issue summonses automatically," he said.
He said ANPR could continue to be used for other purposes, including vehicle identification and smart city applications.
The system forms part of the wider Penang Smart Parking system developed under the vendor's parking management contract, which runs until Dec 31, 2027.
H'ng said any future use of ANPR for parking enforcement would have to take into account conditions on the ground, particularly on Penang island, where narrower roads mean motorists may need to stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
He said the state government was considering measures such as introducing a 10-minute buffer period or conducting multiple scans of a vehicle before an automated compound could be issued.
The Penang government recently instructed MBPP and the Seberang Prai City Council to immediately suspend the implementation of the ANPR system for issuing parking compounds pending a review.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the decision was made after the state government took into account public feedback and views on the system's implementation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Eighth day of wildfires in Indonesian national park
Article:
SURABAYA: Indonesian firefighters backed by helicopters and drones battled devastating flames for an eighth day Monday in a national park on Java Island where over 500 hectares have been lost, an official said.
The blaze has forced the closure of the Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park, a popular tourist destination, and razed an area equivalent to more than 700 football fields.
By Monday, "the fire has spread toward residential areas" in the Dingklik Valley area of the park, East Java disaster mitigation agency official Satriyo Nurseno said.
Two water-bombing helicopters, several fire trucks and drones with sprinklers were aiding forest rangers and soldiers deployed to fight the flames, Satriyo added.
Forestry Minister Raja Juli Antoni said on Sunday it would not be possible to fly cloud-seeding missions to trigger rain over the Bromo area for several days given the lack of clouds.
The process involves spraying particles such as silver iodide and salt into clouds from aircraft to produce rainfall.
Flames devoured more than 500 hectares of land on Mount Bromo in 2023, sparked by a couple lighting a flare during a pre-wedding photo shoot.
Indonesia is forecast to experience a long, intense dry season this year with high risk for drought and wildfires due in part to the El Nino weather phenomenon, the weather agency BMKG has said.
El Nino is a naturally occurring climate phenomenon that brings worldwide changes in winds, air pressure and rainfall patterns.
In India and Southeast Asia, it typically causes drier conditions.
The last El Nino helped make 2023 and 2024 the two hottest years globally on record.
In the first half of this year, more than 107,000 hectares of land burnt countrywide – over twice the area destroyed in wildfires in 2023.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AME Elite to build Wuxi Hyatech facility in Johor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: AME Elite Consortium Bhd, through its unit Pentagon Land Sdn Bhd, has secured a project to build a 220,000 square foot manufacturing facility for Shanghai-listed Wuxi Hyatech Co Ltd in Iskandar Puteri, Johor.
The facility, which will be developed on a 2.75 hectare site within AME Elite's i-TechValley industrial park, will house research, development and production operations for aerospace components and medical orthopaedic implant forgings.
Hyatech, through its Malaysian unit HYA Industry (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd, will use the facility as a key manufacturing base for its broader US$70 million expansion in Southeast Asia.
AME Elite said the project strengthens i-TechValley's portfolio of multinational tenants within the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ).
It also supports Malaysia's push towards advanced manufacturing under the New Industrial Master Plan 2030.
AME Elite executive director and group chief executive officer Dylan Tan Teck Eng said the project reflects the company's ability to deliver customised industrial facilities for high-precision and advanced technology operations.
"Multinational corporations establishing a footprint in Southeast Asia require customised facilities that meet global standards.
"As we deepen our expertise to fulfill the stringent specifications of the aerospace and healthcare sectors, AME Elite is capturing high-value cross-border capital flowing into the JS-SEZ and facilitating greater supply chain resilience," he said.
The latest project builds on AME Elite's track record in the aviation and aerospace sectors, following its recent RM214.1 million contract to construct an aeronautical test cell facility for KLIA Aeropolis Sdn Bhd.
The company is also developing a multi-tenant industrial complex in Subang through a collaboration between Mitsui Fudosan Group and Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd, supporting the aviation, air cargo and maintenance, repair and overhaul sectors.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: How the hard reality of climate change hit Europe's economy this summer
Article:
FOR anyone in Europe who still thought climate change was a problem for future generations, this summer's sweltering heatwaves have brought home the reality that its costly and life-altering economic impacts have already arrived.
Record heat and droughts this summer - which scientists say are exacerbated by global warming - have wreaked havoc in power production, shipping and public health systems, while this wildfire season is on track to be Europe's biggest ever.
Together, the hit to the region's economy can already be measured in the hundreds of billions of euros, economists and academics estimate.
But they warn this is just the beginning, as costs are set to rise faster than temperatures.
Climate is changing more rapidly in Europe than on any other continent and the damage is already stretching public finances, setting off wild swings in inflation, redrawing the tourism map, and forcing the bloc to rethink how power is produced and how goods are transported.
"What makes 2026 particularly worrying from an economic perspective is that there are multiple episodes of extreme events," said University of Mannheim economist Sehrish Usman.
"Take heatwaves, droughts, wildfires... these events are taking place at the same time and mostly in the same regions, compounding their impact," she said.
Temperatures hit records in June and July, and the economic damage will likely exceed all previous marks, economists say.
Traffic on the Rhine and the Danube rivers, key cargo arteries, is severely limited because of low water levels, more than a half dozen nuclear generators have shut or curtailed production due to cooling difficulties.
Agricultural yield estimates have been cut with crops harvested late, such as maize and sunflower, suffering a 6-7 per cent loss already in July.
Heat curtails human productivity and has already claimed tens of thousands of lives, with Germany alone reporting more than 10,000 heat-related deaths.
Meanwhile, the costs of the emergency response, like fighting fires or curtailing power use, further stretch budgets.
[[nid:1508149]]
ING estimates that the halt of traffic on the Rhine alone will lower the GDP of Germany, the world's third-largest economy, by 0.3 percentage points this year, while Hungary's MBH Bank sees a 0.1 percentage point GDP hit for every week the country's largest nuclear generator is offline.
Allianz, the German insurer, estimates the two-week June heatwave alone will cut the GDP of Europe by 0.3 percentage points, and climate change will shave 5-7 per cent off growth by 2030 for the most exposed economies like Spain, France and Italy.
"The total bill for this year will be much larger," said Hazem Krichene, an economist at Allianz. "This figure doesn't account for the fires, droughts, different flood events or the expected El Niño."
Given that the euro zone is expected to grow just one per cent this year, the hit is sizable.
Yet Usman says the full extent of the economic damage will only be felt several years down the line.
"You'd expect the damage to be largest in the year an extreme event happens and then to fade but we find the opposite," Usman said.
"The economic impact grows over the following years because the extreme weather set off a chain of slow economic consequences."
Southern Europe could take the biggest hit as temperature spikes are the largest there, cutting tourism income, exacerbating crop failures and inducing outward migration.
"Can you see tourists marching through southern Italy or Spain in 45 degrees? I can't. So, I think the nature of tourism will change," ING economist Carsten Brzeski said.
The south may get more year-round tourists but summer peaks will drop as vacationers move north, hitting the southern hospitality industry, Brzeski argued.
The south will also take a bigger food price hit from extreme weather, complicating life for the European Central Bank, which is already struggling to keep inflation at target.
"You see bigger effects of extreme temperatures on food prices in places that are already hotter, so if you're in Southern Europe, you'll see a bigger effect," said Maximilian Kotz, a researcher at the Barcelona Supercomputing Center.
[[nid:1508148]]
Extreme heat in 2022 lifted euro zone inflation by 0.34 percentage points via higher food prices, with the south taking a disproportionate hit, Kotz estimated.
Meanwhile, a halt in river transport is making it harder for fuel to reach parts of Europe, widening regional price differences.
"The fiscal consequences fall most heavily on the economies least able to absorb them," Allianz said in a research note.
Reductions in annual tax revenue from lost output could reach 1.8 per cent in France, 1.3 per cent in Italy and Spain as progressive tax systems mean revenues fall faster than output, it estimates.
Business profit margins will also decline, depressing investment and exacerbating the economic loss.
Costs meanwhile surge, both because governments have to fund the emergency response and must invest, such as in future-proofing power generation or transportation routes.
"A key concern is that countries still rely far too much on ad hoc emergency response, which is both expensive and also often quite inefficient," said Heather Grabbe, a senior fellow at the Bruegel think tank.
But investors may push back if governments try to spend more. Debt levels are already high - especially in France and Italy - and countries need to invest in defence and the green energy transition.
The dilemma could draw in the ECB, which bought up trillions of euros worth of countries' debt in the past decade to keep borrowing costs depressed when inflation was too low.
"With such a long list of spending needs, the trend will be towards higher government debt," ING's Brzeski said.
"This will then mean pressure on the ECB to step in and do more quantitative easing, if there is a sudden selloff in bond markets."
* The writer is from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nga confident DAP delegates will vote for country's stability
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: DAP deputy chairman Nga Kor Ming has expressed confidence that party delegates will prioritise national stability when they vote on the party's future in the Federal Government at a special congress on Aug 16.
Nga, who is also Housing and Local Government Minister, said he trusts the more than 4,000 delegates attending the congress to weigh the country's interests carefully before casting their ballots.
"On Aug 16, DAP will have more than 4,000 delegates, I am confident that, as a party that loves the country and has struggled for the past 60 years, the wisdom of more than 4,000 delegates will prevail.
"They will vote according to the interests of the country, safeguard the country's stability and make the wisest choice in line with the country's stability.
That is my belief," he told reporters after launching the National Housing Policy 2026-2035 today.
Nga, however, did not reveal his personal stance or indicate whether he believes DAP's ministers and deputy ministers should retain their posts.
The Aug 16 congress will see delegates
vote by secret ballot
on a motion tabled by the party's central executive committee on whether DAP should continue holding government positions for the remainder of the current parliamentary term.
DAP currently holds five ministerial and seven deputy ministerial posts in the cabinet.
DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke previously said that regardless of the outcome, the party will continue to support Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and remain a member of Pakatan Harapan.
The
special congress
was called following Pakatan Harapan's defeat in the Negeri Sembilan state election on Aug 1, which saw Loke lose the Chennah state seat he had held for 13 years.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bar Council: Refugee repatriation must be voluntary, individually assessed
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Any move to repatriate 5,000 Myanmar refugees must be voluntary and subject to individual risk assessments to ensure no one is returned to persecution or serious harm, the Malaysian Bar Council said.
Its president Anand Raj said the government must uphold the principle of non-refoulement, which prohibits the return of people to a country where their life, freedom or physical safety could be at risk.
He said this should be accompanied by a rights-respecting refugee protection framework developed through meaningful consultation with refugee communities, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and civil society.
"The Bar Council calls upon the government to ensure that any proposal to return the 5,000 Rohingya refugees is based upon individual risk assessment to guarantee that any returns are voluntary, informed, safe and dignified," he said in a statement.
Anand also urged Putrajaya to disclose the key terms of the reported repatriation arrangement with Myanmar, including the screening process and safeguards governing its implementation.
He said the principle of non-refoulement was widely recognised under international law and was increasingly regarded as a fundamental rule that countries could not simply disregard.
"It does not matter that Malaysia is not a State Party to the 1951 Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees or its 1967 Protocol," he said.
Anand said the Malaysian government had itself acknowledged and accepted the principle of non-refoulement since 2015.
The Bar Council cited a Dewan Rakyat Hansard from that year, in which then minister in the Prime Minister's Department Datuk Seri Shahidan Kassim said refugees would not be forcibly returned to their countries of origin.
"As the principle of non-refoulement is increasingly recognised as a rule of jus cogens which is binding upon Malaysia, it is only a matter of time before the Malaysian courts would be called upon to apply non-refoulement as a binding principle of international law," he added.
Anand also called for continued cooperation with the UNHCR during any transition to the government's Refugee Documentation Registration Programme, saying there should be no interruption to the UNHCR's refugee status determination process.
Earlier today, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said Myanmar had
expressed its readiness
to take back 5,000 refugees identified by Malaysia for repatriation, including transporting them home by ship.
The group comprises refugees from Myanmar of various ethnicities and is not limited to the Rohingya community.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Storms from Dolphin soak China's east, disrupt life in Shanghai
Article:
BEIJING: Torrential rain and storms in Typhoon Dolphin's wake have swept through several provinces in China's east, drenching the coastal region and flooding streets in Shanghai, the country's second most populated city.
Dolphin packed maximum sustained winds of 151 km/h near its centre when it made landfall in Zhejiang, the province to the south and west of Shanghai, on Sunday evening before weakening to a tropical storm.
Its remaining rain clouds continued to soak the eastern provinces including Anhui, Jiangsu and Shandong on Monday.
Shanghai's two airports cancelled a total of 943 flights due to the typhoon, reducing capacity by nearly 40 per cent, state broadcaster CCTV said.
Many streets in the suburban Jiading and Qingpu districts around Shanghai's city centre remained waterlogged, according to live-streams shared by residents on social media.
The live videos, not verified by Reuters, showed people wading through knee-high murky water. "It rained almost all night last night.
When I woke up this morning, I found the neighbourhood flooded, and the streets were severely flooded," said 39-year-old Hou Lina, who works in sales in Jiading in Shanghai.
"I've lived in Shanghai for 10 years, and this is the first time I've experienced such inconvenience from a typhoon. This is the first time I've encountered such widespread flooding," she told Reuters.
[[nid:1508129]]
In Shanghai's Jinshan, the district authority said non-essential businesses and organisations could temporarily halt operations, classes, outdoor events and transit services, amid forecasts of continued strong winds and heavy rain on Monday.
Powerful winds and lashing rain flipped over a truck in Zhejiang's Wenzhou, a video posted on TikTok on Sunday showed. It was not clear what happened to the driver.
The strongest typhoon to hit China this year, Dolphin is forecast to move deeper inland to the central provinces of Hubei and Henan in the coming days while also pushing moisture north.
Authorities in the capital Beijing raised warnings for torrential rain and said the city was prepared to activate its flood control response on Tuesday morning.
The typhoon had already travelled 6,000 km before it made landfall, giving it a life-cycle three times longer than an ordinary typhoon, and bringing with it an ultra-large cloud system that enveloped China's east, CCTV said in another report.
Dolphin's impact was also being compared to Doksuri in 2022. That typhoon crossed the country after causing destruction in southeastern Fujian province, unleashing record-breaking rainfall in Beijing.
As the storm clouds meet colder air in the north, Beijing, Tianjin, and Hebei will need to brace for rains into Thursday, CCTV said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Taiwan 'throttles' mobile internet for first time during annual war games
Article:
TAICHUNG: Taiwan slowed the mobile internet in a large swathe of the central part of the island on Monday for the first time during annual war games, simulating communication disruption in the event of a Chinese attack or natural disaster.
Democratically governed Taiwan, which China claims as its own territory, has long lived with the threat of a Chinese invasion and holds air raid drills along with its war games every year, clearing people from the streets for 30 minutes.
During the internet "throttling" drill, centred on Monday on the major central metropolis of Taichung, only basic mobile phone services worked, though key services, from ATMs and traffic signals, were not affected, and neither were landlines nor fixed internet services.
Air raid sirens rang out in Taichung and people cleared the streets from 2.30pm (0630GMT).
The government has widely flagged the drill, sending on Friday afternoon a text message alert to mobile phones across Taiwan in both Chinese and English and posting details on social media.
Northern Taiwan, including the capital Taipei, will see the same exercise on Thursday.
Taiwan's government rejects Beijing's sovereignty claims, saying only the island's people can decide their future.
Earlier on Monday, Taiwan's military simulated repelling a Chinese air landing assault on the strategically vital Penghu Islands.
The 10-day Han Kuang exercise kicked off last week, rehearsing various scenarios should China, which views democratically governed Taiwan as its own territory, ever make good on threats to try and seize the island by force.
Reuters was given rare access to the exercise, observing ground troops loading tank ammunition and taking up firing positions in darkness before the drill began.
Troops from the First Theatre Command opened fire in the pre-dawn hours on a beach in Penghu, which sits in the Taiwan Strait, with M60A3 tanks, various artillery pieces and anti-aircraft guns.
The troops were combining to form what the military called a "multi-layered" defence against a simulated enemy attempting a rapid coastal landing.
Penghu, which sits closer to the coast of the main island of Taiwan than to China, is seen by Taiwanese strategists as a potential first target for Beijing, which could try and take the islands and use them as a base to attack Taiwan with missiles and drones.
Reservists from Penghu took part in the exercise, part of their 14-day training programme as Taiwan's military works to better integrate reserve forces into its operational planning and make its preparations more realistic.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PKR’s Wong Chen resigns Subang parliamentary seat, effective Aug 10, press conference Wednesday
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 10 — PKR’s Wong Chen today confirmed his resignation as Subang MP, effective 5pm.
He said he had met Dewan Rakyat Speaker Johari Abdul on August 5 to hand over his resignation letter, allowing parliamentary officers three working days to prepare for the vacancy.
“We had a gentleman’s agreement not to release any details until August 10 at 5.00pm,” he said in the post.
“We shall also be removing the honorific title of Yang Berhormat from all our billboards, signages and correspondence by next month,” he added.
Wong also announced that he will hold a press conference on Wednesday at 11am.

Title: Housing Ministry resolves RM153b worth of sick or abandoned housing projects, says Nga Kor Ming
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — The Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) has resolved 1,647 “sick” and abandoned private housing projects worth RM153 billion, benefiting nearly 200,000 homebuyers to date, said its Minister Nga Kor Ming.
He said the achievement was the result of efforts by the Special Task Force on Sick and Abandoned Private Housing Projects, established in January 2023 to address the issue and deliver a significant impact to the public.
Nga said the ministry is targeting zero abandoned housing projects by 2030 as part of the national housing sector reform agenda, supported by several mechanisms.
“These mechanisms include the Housing Integrated Management System (HIMS), Transforming and Empowering Data Usage in Housing (TEDUH), the electronic Sale and Purchase Agreement (e-SPA), periodic audits of the Housing Development Account (HDA), and the Option to Purchase (OTP), which will be introduced later this year,” he told reporters after launching the National Housing Policy (DRN) 2026-2035 here today.
Also present were Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar and KPKT Secretary-General Datuk Dr M. Noor Azman Taib.
Nga explained that the OTP mechanism allows developers to withdraw from proceeding with a project within a specified period if sales are sluggish and the project is deemed likely to fail, with buyers receiving a full refund of their deposits.
At the same time, he said buyers would also be given the right to withdraw within a stipulated period, subject to the payment of administrative charges or interest to the developer.
He said the mechanism is expected to reduce the number of abandoned projects while safeguarding consumer interests and the sustainability of the national property industry.
Meanwhile, Nga said the government aimed to build one million affordable homes over 10 years under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), with the target based on actual housing needs and demand determined through big data analytics.
He said artificial intelligence (AI) technology would also be used to identify suitable locations, housing types and price ranges.
On home ownership, Nga said Malaysia’s home ownership rate currently stood at 77 per cent, compared with 42 per cent in Germany, 65 per cent in the United Kingdom and 66 per cent in the United States.
He said the government had allocated RM40 billion through the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP) to assist first-time homebuyers purchasing properties priced up to RM500,000, including gig workers, entrepreneurs and small traders without fixed incomes.
To date, approximately RM18 billion remains available under the scheme, with 17 major financial institutions having agreed to serve as strategic partners.
Nga said about 95,000 individuals, including those from the B40 group, had benefited from the scheme. Eligible applicants are Malaysians aged 18 and above purchasing their first home valued at no more than RM500,000.
Earlier in his speech, Nga said the National Housing Policy (DRN) 2026-2035 reflected the Madani government's commitment to ensuring every citizen had access to quality and affordable housing that supported their well-being.
“Quality housing is not merely about providing shelter; it serves as the foundation for building prosperous families, harmonious communities and sustainable national development,” he said.
The DRN 2026-2035, themed “Humanising Housing”, shifts the focus of housing development from merely building houses to creating high-quality, safe, inclusive, sustainable and liveable communities aimed at enhancing the people’s well-being. — Bernama

Title: Over 600 emergency pumps ready nationwide as Malaysia braces for El Nino, says Irrigation Dept
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — A total of 606 portable emergency pumps of various specifications have been deployed nationwide and are ready to be mobilised as needed to address the El Nino phenomenon.
The Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) said the measure was part of its operational preparedness efforts on the ground when river or dam water levels fell to critical levels.
The portable pumps would be used to channel water supplies to agricultural areas, irrigation schemes and areas experiencing water supply disruptions, as well as to support forest and peatland fire-fighting operations with the Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) and relevant agencies.
“The department also coordinates the integrated use of assets involving federal and state government assets and the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA), while expanding technical assistance to Integrated Agricultural Development Areas (IADA) and other agencies according to current needs.
“Preventive maintenance programmes are carried out regularly to ensure all portable pumps and hydromechanical infrastructure remain in optimal condition before the drought begins. All requests for assistance are coordinated by the department, and the assets can be mobilised to affected locations within 24 hours,” it said.
In line with the national water sector’s digitalisation agenda, the department uses the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system and Pump Tracking System to monitor pump and water gate operations in real time, enabling disruptions or potential damage to be detected early and reducing the risk of water supply disruptions during the El Nino phenomenon.
Previously, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), in its Long Range Weather Outlook updated on July 29, forecast that the El Nino phenomenon would continue until early 2027.
The situation is expected to result in lower rainfall in several areas along the west, east and southern coasts of Peninsular Malaysia, central and western Sarawak, and eastern Sabah, increasing the risk of drought and placing greater pressure on the country's water resources.
DID also said that it was monitoring 56 dams nationwide to ensure the effective integrated management of water resources, agricultural irrigation and flood mitigation, in line with the National Water Policy (DAN) and NADMA Directive No. 1 of 2024.
The monitoring covers dams under the supervision of DID, the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (MAFS), the Sabah Water Department (JANS) and the State Water Regulatory Division (BKSA) through the InfoKemarau Portal and Reservoir Information Management System (RIMS).
“Water releases from dams are carried out in accordance with standard operating procedures (SOPs) to ensure sufficient water supplies for domestic and agricultural use, as well as the safety of the dams. DID also works with state water supply operators to optimise the operation of water intake towers to ensure continuity of water supply to consumers,” it said.
In addition, DID has developed the National Water Balance Management System (NAWABS) as a national water balance management platform to help forecast drought risks and support early mitigation measures by providing projections of water resource availability up to two months ahead and early warnings up to 14 days in advance.
NAWABS currently operates in seven major river basins — Sungai Kedah, Sungai Muda, Sungai Bernam, Sungai Klang, Sungai Melaka, Sungai Kelantan and Sungai Similajau basins — and is expected to be expanded to 12 more river basins by 2028.
“NAWABS information is strengthened through the water resources assessment report prepared weekly by DID.
“The report contains information on river flow rates, dam storage levels and developments in drought conditions, which is shared with NADMA, the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (PETRA), the National Water Services Commission (SPAN), DID top management and state offices,” it said.
The information serves as an important reference for determining mitigation measures, such as coordinating cloud seeding operations, issuing early drought warnings and planning water supply management in affected areas. — Bernama

Title: Any Melaka BN election deal must be made official, says state party chief
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 10 — Any political agreement involving Barisan Nasional (BN) for the Melaka state election must be formally decided and should not be based on speculation or discussions on social media, Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said.
Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka BN chairman, said any negotiations on political cooperation should take into account various factors, including the strengths, weaknesses and advantages of each party before a decision is made.
He said parties interested in forming cooperation with BN for the state election were welcome to hold negotiations, but stressed that such talks would not necessarily result in an alliance.
“Negotiations do not necessarily have to end with the formation of a partnership. Many factors have to be considered before a person or party can become our partner.
