“So I have always stressed that we should not draw conclusions from any unofficial discussions. This time, any agreement must be properly formalised and officially confirmed,” he told reporters at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) in Ayer Keroh here today.
Earlier, Ab Rauf officiated at the August 2026 monthly assembly of the state administration and the launch of the National Month and Jalur Gemilang Flag-Waving Campaign 2026 at the state level.
Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka Umno chairman, said BN would defend the 21 seats it won in the previous state election, while the remaining seven seats could be open for negotiations, including the possibility of seat swaps.
The 15th Melaka state election in 2021 saw BN win 21 of the 28 seats, followed by Pakatan Harapan (PH) with five and Perikatan Nasional (PN) with two.
The mandate of the Melaka state government ends on December 31. — Bernama

Title: Melaka BN free to negotiate, Zahid confirms Ab Rauf empowered to lead coalition seat talks
Article:
GERIK, Aug 10 — Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) has been given the green light to hold discussions with any political coalition ahead of the upcoming Melaka state election.
As reported by
Harian Metro
(HM), BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said he had empowered Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh to lead the talks in search of common ground to ensure stable governance in the state.
“I hope the talks, which are usually complicated when it comes to seat allocations, can be handled amicably. There is no issue that cannot be resolved,” Zahid was quoted as saying.
He added that Ab Rauf, who also chairs Melaka BN and Umno state liaison body, would later present the outcome of the discussions to the coalition’s top leadership before any decision is finalised.
Meanwhile, Zahid, who is also Umno president, said he did not rule out attending PAS’s annual congress if he receives an official invitation, HM reported.
He added that if he is unable to attend personally, Umno would be represented by its leadership team.

Title: Three new housing laws planned as govt reviews Strata Management Act, says Nga Kor Ming
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — The Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) plans to draft and amend four housing laws under the National Housing Policy (DPN) 2026-2035.
The goal is to put in place a legal framework that is more thorough, forward-looking and equitable for all parties.
Minister Nga Kor Ming said the move involves three entirely new laws: the Property Development Act, the Building Managers Act, and the Rent Tenancy Act. In parallel, the government will also revise the existing Strata Management Act 2013.
Speaking to the press after launching the DPN 2026-2035 today, the Minister emphasised that under this new policy, the government is committed to finalising all four Acts as soon as possible.
Also present at the launch were chief secretary to the Government, Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar; attorney general, Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar; and KPKT secretary-general, Datuk Dr. M Noor Azman Taib.
The Minister also provided an update on the Property Development Act, saying it is already in the final stage of review.
He explained that this new law is necessary because the current regulations only cover housing projects, whereas the updated Act will broaden the scope to include commercial real estate as well, such as shop lots and other commercial developments.
Regarding the Building Managers Act, Nga said it is very much needed as Malaysia has nearly three million strata property units across more than 27,000 schemes, including condominiums and SOHO units.
With so many such properties, it is important to have proper rules to make sure they are well maintained, safe, and fit for living.
As for the Rent Tenancy Act, the Minister said this law is meant to create a fair balance between property owners and tenants. It aims to protect the rights and interests of both sides.
He also said the amendment to the Strata Management Act 2013 is necessary to keep up with the changing needs of managing strata properties.
This is important because urbanisation in the country has grown from 28 per cent in 1970 to 78 per cent to date, and is expected to reach 85 per cent by 2040.
Nga also shared that KPKT will roll out a big data analytics system starting next year to solve the problem of mismatched supply and demand in the housing market.
He explained that the system will combine data from state governments, local authorities, and KPKT, broken down by district and locality, as a reference for industry players.
“Our main problem is not supply or construction. The real issue is a mismatch. What is being offered is not what is actually needed, and that is why we have property overhang,” said Nga.
Developers can use the data system to carry out feasibility studies before starting any project. This way, the type, location, and price of the properties they offer will better match what the market actually wants.
He added that using the big data analytics system will not be mandatory for industry players. However, they can choose to subscribe to the system to help them make better decisions.
Nga also said that this approach will allow the definition of affordable housing to be set according to each locality, rather than using a single fixed figure for the whole country.
He pointed out that, based on National Property Information Centre (NAPIC) data, affordable housing in the Klang Valley is around RM500,000, while in Kelantan it is about RM300,000, due to varying income levels.
“As the saying goes, one size does not fit all. Imagine if the price of affordable housing in Kuala Krai, Kelantan, was the same as in Bukit Bintang, Kuala Lumpur. That would not make sense at all,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Doctors confirm elective surgery success, PM Anwar Ibrahim under strict medical watch
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has successfully undergone elective laparoscopic surgery to treat an abdominal para umbilical hernia, his medical team confirmed today.
The procedure was carried out smoothly under the care of specialist doctors.
Anwar is currently undergoing physiotherapy and remains under close observation, Datuk Dr Asri Ranga bin Abdullah Ramaiah, head of the Prime Minister’s medical team, confirmed.

Title: Pakistan PM wishes ‘brother’ Anwar swift recovery from medical procedure
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif wishes Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim a speedy recovery from a medical procedure that the Malaysian leader is slated to undergo today.
He said the people of Pakistan joined him in praying for Anwar’s continued good health and well-being.
“Wishing my dear brother, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, a swift and smooth recovery during his medical procedures.
“May Allah SWT bless him with a speedy return to his duties,” he said in a post on X today.
Earlier, Anwar’s Senior Press Secretary Tunku Nashrul Abaidah said the prime minister was undergoing medical examinations and procedures prescribed by a team of medical specialists.
Anwar is expected to remain under observation for two days. — Bernama

Title: Refunds follow furore as Penang cancels 29,240 ANPR summonses, vows manual enforcement only
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 10 — The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) will cancel 29,240 summonses issued under the automated number plate recognition (ANPR) system between 2025 and August this year.
Penang local government and town and country planning committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye said the city council will also refund a total RM266,160 summons payments that was received in the same period.
“The ANPR summons system has been halted entirely so from now onwards, summons will only be issued manually by the enforcement officers,” he said at a press conference on the issue following public furore over limitations of the system.
He said the state government took into consideration the feedback and concerns raised by the public on the issue.
Among the issues raised were that vehicles which had stopped to drop off passengers were also issued summonses for illegal parking as the ANPR system could not detect if there were drivers and passengers in the vehicles.
“To ensure there are no disputes, all summons issued under the ANPR for illegal parking will be cancelled,” he said.
He said the ANPR system will now be reviewed and will no longer be used for enforcement.
“It will be used only to monitor but enforcement will be conducted manually after this,” he said.
He said those who had already paid the summons can submit their claims from both city councils for refunds by September 30.
As for those who were issued summons for not paying parking fees despite making payment within a 10-minute grace period, they can also submit an appeal for cancellation of the summons and a refund if they have already paid the summons.
They can submit their payment receipts and bank statement to level three in Komtar (MBPP) or email to perbendaharaan@mbpp.gov.my or to the enforcement directorate at MBSP, Level One, Pejabat Cawangan Jalan Betek, 14000 Bukit Mertajam or email to direktorat@mbsp.gov.my.

Title: Amirudin Shari: Pakatan open to working with Bersatu, Perikatan if stability maintained
Article:
BANGI, Aug 10 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) prioritises political stability and the people’s interests when considering any form of political cooperation with other parties or coalitions, said PH Presidential Council member Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
The PKR vice-president said PH remained open to establishing cooperation or reaching an understanding with any party or coalition that upheld these two principles.
“Cooperation with any party, not just Bersatu or Perikatan Nasional (PN), can be considered, provided the underlying principles remain political stability and the well-being of the people,” he said.
Speaking to reporters after officiating the Ecology International Conference II (HEIC-II) 2026 here today, the Selangor Menteri Besar also denied that Selangor PH had entered into any cooperation with Bersatu, stressing that no discussions or decisions involving the party had taken place.
Amirudin said any potential cooperation must be evaluated rationally at the central level, taking into consideration factors such as the timing of elections and other relevant circumstances.
“Of course, I cannot decide on my own, as I also share responsibility with the central leadership.
“So, if there are discussions (at the Selangor PH level), I will bring the matter to the central leadership. What exists currently are merely external ideas or views, which may stem from political realignments at the national level or in the context of a state election,” he said.
Last Friday, media reports indicated that Selangor PH appeared open to the possibility of collaborating with Bersatu, particularly at the state level.
The alignment is believed to be aimed at ensuring both parties remain relevant and strong ahead of upcoming elections, including the general election (GE) and the Melaka state election. — Bernama

Title: The death of plastic? E-wallets now displacing credit and debit cards across Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — Malaysia’s move away from cash has a clear winner. According to Ipsos Malaysia’s newly released E-Wallet Landscape 2026 report, e-wallets are only growing, but are supplanting debit and credit cards as Malaysians’ preferred non-cash payment method.
The numbers, drawn from a nationally representative Ipsos survey of 1,029 Malaysians aged 18-74 fielded in April 2026, tell a stark story of substitution over the past four years.
E-wallet usage among non-cash payment users climbed from 52 per cent in 2023 to 81 per cent in 2026 — a jump of nearly 30 percentage points.
Over the same period, debit card usage fell from 76 per cent to 56 per cent, and credit card usage nearly halved, from 15 per cent down to 9 per cent. Online banking and digital transfers held comparatively steady, moving from 70 per cent to 70 per cent.
As e-wallets rose, cards fell — while online banking, arguably a complementary rather than competing habit, stayed roughly flat.
Generational infrastructure shift
Ipsos frames this as more than incremental change. Overall non-cash payment adoption among Malaysians has climbed steadily too — from 51 per cent of the population in 2023 to 72 per cent in 2026 — meaning e-wallets are not simply taking share from a shrinking cashless pie; they are the primary engine expanding that pie in the first place, while simultaneously eating into cards’ share within it.
The report credits Bank Negara Malaysia’s push to strengthen the digital payment ecosystem, alongside the rollout of interoperable QR payment infrastructure (such as DuitNow QR, which lets a single QR code work across competing wallet apps), as key enablers.
That interoperability removes a major historical advantage cards held — universal acceptance — since a shopper no longer needs to worry whether a merchant accepts a specific wallet brand.
The displacement is most visible in everyday, in-person spending rather than online transactions. Ipsos data shows sharp usage growth for e-wallets at food and beverage outlets, tolls and parking, and retail stores — precisely the point-of-sale moments where a debit or credit card would traditionally have been tapped or swiped.
Bill payments (70 per cent) and money transfers (65 per cent) also rank among the top e-wallet use cases, encroaching further on territory once dominated by online banking and standing instructions tied to bank cards.
More competition
For banks and card issuers, the implications are significant: falling card usage can mean reduced interchange fee income and weaker card-linked product engagement, even as many wallets (like MAE) are themselves bank-owned, meaning some of this shift is a case of banks competing with their own card businesses rather than losing out entirely.
For everyday Malaysians, particularly those who have relied on a physical debit or credit card for decades, the practical takeaway is that acceptance and convenience have now tipped decisively toward wallets for routine spending — though cards likely retain an edge for larger purchases, credit-building, and online transactions requiring buyer protections that wallets don’t always offer.
Ipsos’s own assessment is unambiguous: Malaysia has moved “beyond digital payment adoption to digital payment dependence” — and for businesses and banks alike, sitting outside that ecosystem is no longer a viable option.

Title: High Court upholds blogger Jufazli Shi’s acquittal over YouTube post against Ismail Sabri, Umno
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — The High Court here today upheld the acquittal of blogger Jufazli Shi Ahmad on two charges of posting offensive communications against former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob and UMNO on YouTube and failing to provide police with the password to the account four years ago.
Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin upheld the Sessions Court’s decision after dismissing the prosecution’s appeal against Jufazli’s acquittal on October 18, 2024, at the end of the prosecution’s case.
“After reading the appeal record, the grounds of judgment of the Sessions Court judge and the submissions of both parties, this court dismisses the appellant’s appeal and upholds the decision of the Sessions Court judge to discharge and acquit the appellant,” Aslam said.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Mohamad Fadhly Mohd Zamry appeared for the prosecution, while Jufazli was represented by lawyer Ramesh N.P. Chandran.
Jufazli was charged with creating and initiating the transmission of an offensive communication in the form of a video with intent to annoy another person through his ‘King Maker Politik’ account on YouTube at 3pm on June 27, 2022.
The link to the offensive video was accessed at 3pm at the Criminal Investigation Division office of the Dang Wangi District Police Headquarters (IPD) on July 1, 2022.
The charge was framed under Section 233(1)(a) of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 and is punishable under Section 233(3) of the same Act, which provides for a maximum fine of RM50,000 or imprisonment for up to one year, or both, upon conviction, and a further fine of RM1,000 for each day the offence continues after conviction.
Jufazli was also charged with failing to provide the password to his ‘King Maker Politik’ YouTube account, which was stored on his mobile phone, to a police officer at the Dang Wangi IPD at 12.10pm on July 5 the same year.
The charge was framed under Section 249 of the same Act, which carries a maximum fine of RM100,000 or imprisonment for up to two years, or both, upon conviction. — Bernama

Title: Prevention is better than cure: Govt unveils OTP exit clause to stop sick housing projects
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — The government aims to ensure Malaysia has no abandoned housing projects by 2030, with a new Option to Purchase (OTP) mechanism expected to give developers and buyers an earlier avenue to withdraw from projects that may no longer be viable.
Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said the mechanism was part of a broader housing reform agenda aimed at preventing projects from becoming sick or abandoned in the first place.
“Prevention is better than cure. That is why I have implemented housing reforms so that our mission is to ensure that by 2030, Malaysia has no more abandoned projects,” Nga said at a separate press conference following the launch of the National Housing Policy 2026-2035.
Nga said the ministry’s special task force on private-sector sick and abandoned housing projects had resolved 1,647 such projects — as of today — involving RM153 billion and nearly 200,000 homebuyers over the past three years.
Among the reforms included in this policy are the Housing Integrated Management System (HIMS), the Transforming & Empowering Data Usage in Housing (Teduh) platform, electronic sales and purchase agreements, regular audits of Housing Development Accounts, a new Housing Development Act, as well as the introduction of an OTP and Sunset Clause.
Nga said the OTP mechanism was expected to be introduced by the end of this year.
He said the mechanism could provide both developers and buyers with an avenue to withdraw from a project within a specified period under agreed terms.
“For example, we give a period of six months. If within those six months the developer feels that the project is going to fail, the developer will have the right to offer an exit,” he said.
Under the proposed mechanism, deposits paid by buyers would be returned in full under such circumstances, together with the applicable terms set out in the agreement, he said.
Buyers could also exercise their right to withdraw during the specified period if they found a more suitable property, subject to charges and other terms under the agreement.
Nga said the mechanism was intended to allow both sides to reassess their position at an earlier stage instead of allowing an unviable project to progress until it became a larger problem.
“If there is no OTP, a developer may have to continue building. Once construction has started, even if sales are not there, they have to complete the project,” he said.
He said a developer could otherwise continue construction on a large project despite weak sales, eventually running into financial difficulties and leave buyers and the government to deal with the consequences.
Nga said HIMS, Teduh, regular HDA account audits and OTP formed part of a package of reforms being actively implemented by the ministry.
“I will monitor this every month to ensure that by 2030, our country has no more abandoned projects,” he said.
He said housing needs could be assessed according to individual districts and locations, including the number and types of homes required.
The system would also take into account local income levels and property prices, allowing housing supply and prices to better reflect conditions in different areas.
Nga said developers would eventually be able to subscribe to the system and use the information when planning projects, although its use would not be mandatory.
He stressed that all new housing projects would continue to be subject to requirements for developers to obtain advertising permits and developer licences.
“The government would not simply issue developer licences and would use available information to assess whether proposed projects were appropriate for the market,” he said, adding that the approach was intended to help create a more balanced property market while reducing the risk of future oversupply.
Nga also said the government needed to balance housing affordability with the need for property values to appreciate over time.
“Property ownership is not only wealth preservation. It is also wealth creation,” he said.
He said the government did not want house prices to spike, but neither should property values remain stagnant for decades.
“What we want is a gradual increase,” he said.
On housing affordability for the M40 group, Nga said lower home ownership rates could be influenced by various factors and should not automatically be attributed to affordability alone.
He said some people, particularly younger people and graduates, may prefer to rent rather than commit to long-term bank financing.
“We respect your choice and your option,” he said.
Nga said the government would therefore provide options for those who wanted to own homes while also developing a more structured rental market.
The National Housing Policy 2026-2035, launched today, proposes the enactment of a Residential Tenancy Act to create a more transparent, secure and balanced rental market.
Nga said the government’s approach was to provide housing choices according to people’s circumstances, whether they preferred to own or rent.
The policy also includes the phased implementation of the Build-Then-Sell (BTS) system to strengthen protection for homebuyers.

Title: Selangor govt to local councils: Don’t let land go idle, put it to use for urban farming
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 10 — Local authorities in Selangor have been urged to identify vacant plots of land to prevent them from falling into neglect or being occupied by unauthorised parties, including foreign nationals.
State Infrastructure and Agriculture Committee chairman Datuk Izham Hashim said applications could be made to lease the identified land for urban farming activities, including community gardens and programmes carried out by the private sector.
He said the move would enable vacant urban land to be managed more systematically while optimising its use for high-value agricultural activities.
“The state government has directed local government authorities (PBT) to identify idle land and apply for leases so that the sites can be utilised for community gardens, agricultural programmes or by interested private parties.
“This includes making the land available to PKPS (Selangor Agricultural Development Corporation) for agricultural programmes, ensuring that the land is used in a more organised and systematic manner,” he told the State Legislative Assembly sitting here today.
Izham was responding to a supplementary question from Muhamad Izuan Ahmad Kasim (PH-Kota Damansara) on a proposal to use idle land for urban agriculture as a measure to prevent such areas from being occupied by foreign nationals.
He said the Petaling Jaya City Council was among the local authorities that had implemented the initiative in stages.
Meanwhile, Izham said the Urban Agriculture Programme (Community Gardens) continued to receive encouraging responses, with the number of projects increasing from 39 involving 390 participants in 2024 to 66 projects involving 990 participants in 2025.
He added that agricultural produce from the programme increased from 33.6 tonnes to 49.9 tonnes during the same period, while more than 200 community garden sites had been established within local authority areas.
He said the development not only encouraged greater community participation in urban agriculture but also helped increase food production at the community level and strengthen Selangor’s food security agenda. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak schools told to suspend outdoor activities if API exceeds 100
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 10 — All schools in Sarawak have been urged to continuously monitor Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in their respective areas amid the transboundary haze currently affecting the state.
The Sarawak Education Department (JPNS) said all educational institutions under its purview had been instructed to postpone all outdoor activities if the weather was too hot.
It said in areas where API readings exceeded 100, all outdoor activities involving students must be suspended.
“Educational institutions must stay updated on developments through the media regarding the haze situation in their respective areas or districts and comply with the recommendations of the Ministry of Health from time to time,” JPNS said in a statement today.
The department also advised students to wear face masks and drink adequate amounts of water frequently to regulate their body temperature.
“Schools should also ensure an adequate supply of clean drinking water and encourage students to bring their own drinking water.
“They should also remain vigilant and cooperate with nearby clinics and hospitals in the event of any complications involving students due to hot weather,” it said.
The number of areas in Sarawak recording unhealthy API readings due to transboundary haze rose to nine this morning.
Based on the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), the areas were Kuching (161), Samarahan (161), Serian (179), Sri Aman (155), Sarikei (155), Sibu (158), Mukah (156), Bintulu (142) and Samalaju (141).
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are hazardous.
API data is updated hourly based on readings from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide. — Bernama

Title: Five men remanded another week over murder of Batu Pahat businessman found in fishing net
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Aug 10 — Five men, who are being investigated in connection with the murder of a businessman here, have been remanded for another week.
Magistrate Aimi Nawwar Mohamad Othman granted the remand extension for all the suspects, aged between 26 and 40, at the Magistrate’s Court here today until Monday.
Their remand is to assist investigators who are probing the murder of a 39-year-old businessman whose bound body was found floating in Sungai Tanjung Sembrong in Parit Raja here last week.
The five suspects were previously in police custody and were remanded for seven days to assist investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
Their initial remand application ended today.
On August 3, the body of the businessman was found floating along the river by members of the public.
The body was tied up and bound in a fishing net.
Initial investigations revealed that the victim was believed to have been killed by strangulation with a rope around his neck before both of his hands were tied with tape.
Police believe that the victim’s body was tied in a fishing net with five rocks before being thrown into the river.
Investigators believe that the rocks were used to submerge the deceased’s remains to prevent them from rising to the surface.
The victim was a businessman from Mutiara Rini in Iskandar Puteri and had been reported missing since July 29.
He was identified by his next of kin based on his clothing and personal belongings.
Of the five men arrested, two had prior records related to crime and narcotics.

Title: Terengganu MB says Jalur Gemilang flown without crescent moon and star was ‘unintentional’, ‘isolated’ incident
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 10 — Terengganu Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar said the display of a Jalur Gemilang without its crescent and star at Dataran Batu Buruk was an isolated incident and was not deliberate.
Berita Harian
reported that he said the state government would investigate the matter after a video of the flag circulated on social media on Friday.
“I think this was not deliberate; it was an isolated and unintentional case,” he was quoted as saying.
Ahmad Samsuri said steps would also be taken to prevent a recurrence, regardless of whether the flag had been put up by the authorities or members of the public.
He was speaking after officiating the Terengganu-level World Ranger Day 2026 celebration at Wisma Darul Iman.
Kuala Terengganu mayor Lizan Che Mat, meanwhile, said the flag originally had the crescent and star, but the section bearing the symbols had come loose from its stitching following strong winds.
He said the Kuala Terengganu City Council (MBKT) removed the flag as soon as the issue was detected on Friday and replaced it with a new one.
He said MBKT would stop using stitched flags of that type and would instead buy fully finished flags to reduce the risk of a similar incident.
Lizan added that the council took the matter seriously and would ensure flags under its care were in good condition and complied with the required specifications.

Title: Chief secretary to govt wishes Anwar happy 79th birthday
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — Chief Secretary to the Government (KSN) Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar today wished Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim a happy 79th birthday.
He also prayed that the Prime Minister will always be blessed with good health, strength and wisdom in leading the country.
“Insya-Allah, we in the civil service will continue to steadfastly support the aspirations and reform agenda of the public service for the people and the country,” he said in a Facebook post.
The Prime Minister’s Office also conveyed similar birthday wishes through a video uploaded on Facebook, saying:
“Efforts continue, the trust is fulfilled, and to Allah SWT we place our trust.”
Meanwhile, the Malaysia Madani Facebook page also prayed that the Prime Minister would always be under Allah SWT’s protection.
“Happy birthday to YAB PMX. May you continue to be blessed with the strength to contribute to and work tirelessly for the country and the nation,” it posted. — Bernama

Title: Bukit Aman busts violent kidnapping syndicate preying on foreigners, discovers unknown victim after shootout
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department said today it succeeded in taking down a violent kidnapping syndicate that preyed on foreign nationals following a joint investigation with the Singapore Police Force.
The crackdown culminated in a shootout between police and suspects, leading to the rescue of two abducted victims — a Singaporean national who works as a retirement consultant, and a Chinese national woman.
Following the raid, CID director Commissioner Datuk M. Kumar said six individuals in their 30s comprising five men and one woman were arrested. Among those detained are one local Malaysian who is part of the criminal group, while the remaining five suspects are Chinese nationals.
“Their modus operandi was to look for victims through WeChat,” Commissioner Kumar said at a press conference at the Bukit Aman Federal Police Headquarters here.
“They pretended to offer high-paying jobs or social escorts. Once they get a response a meeting is set with the targets and then they get kidnapped,” he added.
During the operation, officers recovered two handguns and a machete.
The raiding team also found a second victim, a woman. Commissioner Kumar said the police was surprised to find the woman in separate room since the raid was initially planned only to rescue the Singaporean national.
The woman is a Chinese national, and no police report was lodged regarding her kidnapping.
Investigations revealed that prior to the rescue, SG$ 15,000 (RM49,600) had already been paid to the syndicate in three separate tranches for the Singaporean victim.
The kidnappers had also demanded a ransom of US$ 20,000 (RM89,000) for the Chinese national woman, but no payment was made.
Subsequent drug screenings showed that the arrested local suspect tested negative, while four of the male China nationals tested positive. All six suspects have been remanded from August 7 to August 14 to assist with ongoing investigations.
Police believe the syndicate is also linked to at least two other kidnapping cases in Kuala Lumpur.
The case came to light after another victim managed to break free from the captors and lodged a police report.
Police have urged the public to exercise extreme caution on social media platforms, warning against accepting job or meeting offers from strangers or agreeing to meet individuals met online.

Title: Govt unveils housing policy shift, big data to cut oversupply and drive affordable homes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — Housing development will be planned according to local needs and market demand starting next year to reduce unsold homes under the new National Housing Policy 2026-2035 (DRN 2026-2035).
Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said the shift towards more data-driven planning was among the key changes under the policy, which seeks to address the mismatch between housing supply and demand while expanding access to affordable home ownership.
“Starting next year, housing development will be planned according to local needs, location and market demand. Through this approach, we hope to reduce the oversupply of unsold properties in the future,” Nga said in his address during the launch of the National Housing Policy 2026-2035 today.
Themed “Humanising Housing”, the policy is aimed at addressing challenges including rising living costs, demographic changes, mismatches between housing supply and demand, unsold properties, as well as delayed, sick and abandoned housing projects.
It comprises six focus areas, 17 strategies and 59 action plans, with a target of providing one million affordable homes by 2035 through a more comprehensive, integrated and data-driven approach.
The policy also seeks to ensure that affordable housing prices are better aligned with local incomes and the needs of residents.
At a separate press conference, Nga said big data analytics would allow housing needs to be assessed according to individual districts and locations, including the number and types of homes required.
He said the system would also take into account local income levels and property prices, allowing the definition of affordable housing to better reflect differences between areas.
“Imagine having an affordable home in Kuala Krai, Kelantan, at the same price as one in Bukit Bintang, Kuala Lumpur. That is not scientific. That is why we need big data analytics,” he said.
Nga said developers would eventually be able to subscribe to the system and use the data when planning projects, although its use would not be mandatory.
He said the system could help developers determine the type of housing, price and location that would better match local demand.
“If big data analytics shows that a particular district needs 5,000 housing units, with different types of homes, developers can refer to the big data analytics when planning their projects,” he said.
Nga said the system would combine data from relevant agencies and the Housing and Local Government Ministry (KPKT) before being made available to industry players.
He said artificial intelligence would also support the system by helping identify suitable housing products, prices and locations based on local conditions.
“We cannot set a target of one million homes if there is no need for them. That is why big data analytics comes in,” he said.
“We set the target to ensure Malaysians have homes according to their respective needs and affordability.”
Nga said changing socio-economic circumstances, including the growing number of people earning through the gig economy, entrepreneurship, flexible employment and digital businesses, meant housing financing also needed to evolve.
“The employment landscape today has changed, requiring a more inclusive financing approach that is suited to current realities,” he said.
The government will strengthen existing instruments such as the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP), which has a RM40 billion facility.
Nga said 95,000 first-time homebuyers had benefited from SJKP so far, with the ministry aiming to assist 100,000 first-time buyers through the scheme.
The policy will also expand access to home ownership through mechanisms including Rent-to-Own (RTO), Shared Ownership, Fixed Rate Mortgage (FRM) and SJKP.
“These approaches are aimed at expanding opportunities for home ownership among more Malaysians without relying on just one financing model,” Nga said.
The policy also proposes the enactment of a Residential Tenancy Act to establish a more comprehensive regulatory framework for the rental market and create a fairer relationship between tenants and landlords.
Nga said the ministry was preparing the proposed legislation to create a more transparent, secure and balanced residential rental market.
Another focus is transit-oriented development (TOD), with the government seeking to provide housing with better access to public transport.
Nga said Malaysia had invested billions of ringgit in public transport infrastructure and housing development should help optimise its use, particularly among lower-income groups.
“It is time for housing development to encourage and optimise the use of public transport,” he said.
He said better access to public transport could reduce reliance on private vehicles while supporting Malaysia’s aspiration to achieve a carbon-neutral economy by 2050.
The DRN 2026-2035 will also promote the use of modern construction technologies, including artificial intelligence, big data analytics, Building Information Modelling (BIM), Industrialised Building System (IBS) and Prefabricated Prefinished Volumetric Construction (PPVC).
Nga said technology could improve productivity and speed up project delivery while helping the government make more accurate decisions.
“Modern technology is not merely about increasing the efficiency of the industry. It also helps the government make more accurate decisions, reduce wastage and ensure homes can be completed faster and with better quality,” he said.
At the same time, the DRN 2026-2035 places greater emphasis on housing that is inclusive and age-friendly, including meeting the needs of senior citizens and people with disabilities.
Nga said housing planning needed to take into account the needs of older Malaysians so they could continue to live active, independent, comfortable and safe lives in age-friendly communities.
The policy also seeks to strengthen the management of strata communities.
Malaysia currently has nearly three million strata property units across more than 27,000 strata schemes.
Nga said problems such as water leaks, poor cleanliness, poorly maintained public facilities and weak management could directly affect residents’ quality of life and property values.
“We need to ensure that every strata community is managed efficiently, transparently and responsibly so that residents and property owners can enjoy a more comfortable, safe and quality environment,” he said.
The government will strengthen strata management through amendments to the Strata Management Act 2013 (Act 757), while strengthening the accountability and governance of Joint Management Bodies (JMBs), Management Corporations (MCs) and Commissioners of Buildings (COBs).
Nga said every strategy and action plan under the policy would be supported by efficient governance, continuous monitoring and close cooperation with state governments, local authorities, financial institutions, industry players, professional bodies and other stakeholders.
He added the policy would also be reviewed and improved from time to time to ensure it remained responsive to changes in demographics, technology and the economy, as well as the needs of the people.
“DRN 2026-2035 is not merely a development plan for the housing sector, but also a commitment by the Madani Government to ensure every citizen has access to quality, affordable housing that supports their well-being,” Nga said.
“Quality housing is not merely about providing shelter, but also forms the foundation for prosperous families, harmonious communities and sustainable national development.”
The DRN 2026-2035 is expected to serve as the main reference document for ministries, agencies, state governments, local authorities and industry players in planning and implementing national housing development through 2035.

Title: Sanusi says Kedah may hold Penang ‘lease’ claim until Perikatan takes Putrajaya
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Aug 10 — Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor reportedly said the state is considering delaying its claim for higher Penang “lease” payments, and instead wait for a Perikatan Nasional (PN) takeover of the federal government.
According to
The Star
, Sanusi said Putrajaya had yet to respond positively to Kedah’s demand despite the state pursuing a review of the payments for the past six years.
“If the federal government remains stubborn and refuses to pay or consider Kedah’s application, we will change the federal government,” he was quoted as saying.
“We are considering whether all these documents should be submitted now for discussion or later, after we become the federal government.”
Sanusi said Kedah had pursued a review for the past six years and had raised the matter with then prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin during the PN administration, but the supporting documents were not ready for a formal submission at the time.
He said the state had since completed a study by historians and legal experts examining historical documents, agreements, payment records and the legal and constitutional basis of its claim, with the final report presented to state leaders on April 15 last year.
Kedah has said it is seeking RM300 million annually from the federal government, which has paid the state an annual RM10 million special contribution since 2018 in addition to the longstanding RM10,000 payment provided for under Article 167(7) of the Federal Constitution.
Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said last month that the matter fell under federal jurisdiction and that his state government had not received any legal correspondence from Kedah over the claim.

Title: Penang grants Jelutong landfill extension until Oct 2026, project faces scrutiny over EIA concerns
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 10 — The Penang state government has granted PLB Engineering Berhad (PLBE) an extension of time (EOT) until October 18 for its proposed RM1 billion Jelutong landfill rehabilitation and development project.
State Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye said the developer’s application for an extension was presented to the state executive council on August 5.
“Based on the presentation, the state government decided that an extension of time be granted until October 18, 2026,” he said in a statement today.
The project involves the proposed safe closure of the Jelutong landfill, the provision of a new site for the disposal of construction waste and marine clay, as well as development of the rehabilitated site.
H’ng said the extension was granted to allow PLBE to complete the remaining processes and fulfil conditions and requirements imposed by the relevant technical agencies.
He said the decision also took into account the agreed project plans and the interests and requirements of all parties involved.
“The state government will continue to closely monitor the implementation of this project to ensure that all conditions and obligations are fully complied with by the developer in accordance with technical and legal requirements and in the public interest,” he said.
The latest extension comes amid scrutiny over the proposed rehabilitation of the landfill and reclamation off Karpal Singh Drive, including questions over the project’s environmental impact assessment (EIA).
In June, Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the state government had met with the Department of Environment (DoE) to better understand the considerations surrounding the EIA application for the project.
At the time, Chow said the DoE had accepted another EIA application from the developer and stressed that the state needed to go through the proper process before reaching a decision.
Non-governmental organisation Protect Karpal Singh Drive Action Committee, had previously questioned whether the developer under the Jelutong Landfill Joint Development Agreement was receiving “exceptional accommodations”.
The group had raised concerns over repeated extensions of time, revisions to payment structures and the scale of the proposed coastal reclamation.
It also questioned whether the financial restructuring and continued extensions were justified in light of previous EIA rejections and delays in the commencement of the project.

Title: High Court requests decision on venue for judicial review involving Negeri Sembilan Undang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — The High Court has ordered counsel for three former Negeri Sembilan Undang and the incumbent Johol Undang to decide whether their judicial review will proceed here or Seremban, to avoid the risk of conflicting rulings on the same matter.
High Court judge Norliza Othman’s directive follows an earlier originating summons filed by the applicants at the Seremban High Court in May, which has yet to be heard,
The Edge
reported.
Counsel Mohd Khairul Azam Aziz, of Messrs Azam Aziz, was instructed to seek instructions from his clients on the matter. All parties are scheduled to return to court on Oct 7 to provide an update.
During the proceedings, the court also declined an oral application by Mohd Khairul for a gag order to prohibit public discussion of the case. The application was opposed by the Dewan Keadilan and Undang (DKU) and the Negeri Sembilan government, who argued that the proceedings involve matters of public interest.
The court has not yet ruled on a pending application by the DKU to intervene in the case; this decision remains deferred until Oct 7.
The applicants — Datuk Mubarak Thahak, Datuk Maarof Mat Rashid, Datuk Abd Rahim Yasin, and Datuk Muhammed Abdullah — have named the Negeri Sembilan menteri besar (MB) and the state government as respondents.
In their judicial review application filed on July 17, the quartet is seeking a mandamus order to compel the MB to sign a proclamation document. This document seeks the removal of the present Yang di-Pertuan Besar, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawer, and a further proclamation naming Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Jaafar as the 12th Yang di-Pertuan Besar. The applicants are requesting that the MB sign the document within seven days of the court order.
Separately, the four Undang, along with Tunku Besar Tampin Tunku Syed Razman and Datuk Seri Badarudin Abdul Khalid, filed an originating summons in the Seremban High Court in May. They are seeking a court order for the production of DKU minutes dated April 17, following the expulsion of Datuk Mubarak, a decision they are also challenging.
The DKU and its secretary, Raja Norazli Raja Nordin, have opposed this application, arguing that DKU matters are non-justiciable and outside the court's jurisdiction. Consequently, the court refused a stay over the decision to remove Datuk Mubarak.
In a related development, Seremban High Court judge Roz Mawar Rozain granted leave on July 8 for a committal hearing against the six applicants for the alleged violation of an ad-interim injunction.
The violation pertains to the holding of a DKU meeting and participation in the installation of Tunku Nadzaruddin on June 5. These committal proceedings are currently stayed pending an appeal at the Court of Appeal.
Senior federal counsel Nurhafizza Azizan appeared for the Attorney General’s Chambers, while David Mathew appeared for the DKU.

Title: Akmal Nasrullah unveils RM12.3m Penang STEM programme, targeting 100,000 students by 2030
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 10 — The federal government will allocate RM12.3 million for a four-year STEM talent programme in Penang aimed at reaching 100,000 students by 2030.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the allocation will support the implementation of the Penang STEM Talent Blueprint, which was first introduced by Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow in 2024.
“We appreciate the efforts undertaken by Penang, so we agreed to collaborate with the target of training 100,000 students by 2030 as part of our efforts to promote interest in STEM,” he told a press conference after launching the STEM Talent Pilot Project here today.
He said the Economy Ministry had agreed to provide RM12.3 million over four years to implement the programme, which will expose students to science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) from an early age.
The pilot programme is a collaboration between the Economy Ministry and the Penang government to strengthen the talent pipeline needed by future industries.
Akmal said the programme will comprise four streams covering different levels of schooling, “Ignite: STEM Education” and “Ignite: MathQuest” for primary school students, “Embed: AI on Wheels” for lower secondary students, and “Embed: Technical Skill Learning” for upper secondary students.
The programmes were developed by Tech Dome Penang, Penang Math Platform, Penang Science Cluster and Penang STEM.
Akmal said Penang’s established industrial ecosystem made it an ideal location to test a model that could later be replicated elsewhere in the country.
“At the national level, we see that this whole-of-ecosystem approach to cultivating interest in STEM can be made a pilot project in Penang and, based on its success, subsequently introduced in other states,” he said.
He said the programme was not merely about increasing students’ interest in science and mathematics but about ensuring that local youths could participate in the higher-value economic opportunities being created around them.
Akmal said Penang already has a strong specialisation in the electrical and electronics (E&E), semiconductor and high-tech manufacturing sectors, making talent development increasingly important to sustain its industrial growth.
He said Penang’s economy grew by 7.3 per cent in 2025, compared with national gross domestic product growth of 5.2 per cent, while the state’s manufacturing sector expanded by 10 per cent.
Penang’s GDP reached RM130.3 billion, while the state accounted for 48.9 per cent of Malaysia’s total exports in June this year.
Akmal said technological advancement must be accompanied by efforts to ensure that local communities are not left behind.
“Talent development needs to begin earlier, from primary school to secondary school, and be strengthened through higher education, TVET and industrial training,” he said.
“When we talk about STEM at school level, it is not merely about mathematics or science. STEM shapes how our children think, how they solve problems, and subsequently builds their confidence and prepares them to go further,” he said.
The programme will also give particular attention to rural schools and lower-income communities, with students receiving hands-on exposure to emerging fields including artificial intelligence (AI), data science, robotics and digital technologies.
Akmal said 86 per cent of employers expect AI and information-processing technologies to change how businesses operate.
“Technology is moving so rapidly out there. We need to equip our children with the skills to adapt to technologies, jobs and challenges that are constantly changing, so that they can remain relevant,” he said.
Akmal said Malaysia also needs to develop 60,000 skilled engineers as the country seeks to move further up the semiconductor value chain from back-end activities towards higher-value front-end activities.
He said Malaysia’s next phase of industrial development should be about creating technology rather than merely manufacturing products developed elsewhere.
“Previously, we were proud when we successfully produced goods that were ‘made in Malaysia’. Now, we want to change that to ‘made by Malaysia’,” he said.
“It is not merely about putting factories here, but having our own talent create higher value,” he said.
He said the government ultimately wanted the students exposed to the programme to become more than workers equipped for future industries.
“We are no longer just clients or consumers. We are the innovators. We are the inventors that will change the landscape of technology even on the global stage,” he said.
Meanwhile, Chow thanked the Economy Ministry for backing the state’s STEM blueprint and providing the RM12.3 million allocation.
He said Penang had already implemented various STEM initiatives to support the state’s economic development, including programmes involving industry placements and new skills training.
“We have received good collaboration from industry, and many programmes involving the placement of students in industries are already taking place,” he said.
Chow said one of the aims was to equip students with practical skills from as early as Form Four, giving them the option of entering the workforce after completing their Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM).
“Part of our aspiration is that students who have completed their SPM can already start working because this programme prepares them from Form Four onwards,” he said.
Akmal also called on companies to go beyond supporting formal STEM modules by giving students first-hand exposure to workplaces and new technologies.
“If there is an opportunity, bring our children to your workplaces and show them what new technologies you are actually acquiring,” he said.
He added that the effectiveness of the Penang pilot will be evaluated and improved before it is considered for expansion to other states and economic sectors nationwide.

Title: Anthony Loke steps aside after 22 years, Arul Kumar appointed Negeri Sembilan DAP chairman
Article:
SEREMBAN, Aug 10 — Nilai assemblyman and National DAP vice-chairman J. Arul Kumar has been appointed as the new Negeri Sembilan DAP chairman, effective today.
DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said the state committee unanimously selected Arul Kumar after he stepped down from the position, which he had held for 22 years since 2004.
“Arul Kumar’s appointment is a very positive development and demonstrates that DAP is a multiracial party. We assess individuals based on their qualifications and ability to lead,” he said.
Loke also expressed confidence in the new state committee, describing its members as experienced, united and accustomed to working together.
“Most importantly, we will continue serving every constituency we represent with dedication,” he told a press conference after chairing the Negeri Sembilan DAP state committee meeting.
Loke said Arul Kumar, previously the Negeri Sembilan DAP vice-chairman, was appointed in accordance with the party constitution.
Loke said he would remain a member of the Negeri Sembilan DAP committee while continuing as the party’s secretary-general.
He said leading the state chapter carried significant responsibility, particularly after DAP performed strongly in the previous four state elections and retained nine seats in the recent 16th Negeri Sembilan election.
Loke stepped down as state chairman with effect from today after failing to defend the Chennah seat.
He said Arul Kumar’s appointment as his successor reflected DAP’s commitment to multiracial politics, although most members of the state committee are Chinese.
Arul Kumar is not the first Indian leader to head Negeri Sembilan DAP.  Loke noted that Malay leader Yusof Bador had also served as state chairman in the early 1980s.
Meanwhile, Arul Kumar is expected to pay a courtesy call on Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim soon to discuss a new framework for cooperation between the state government and the opposition.
Arul Kumar described his appointment as a major responsibility and pledged to ensure that DAP continued providing the best possible service to the public.
He said the party would serve residents in the nine constituencies it won while continuing to assist those in Chennah and Repah, which it no longer represents.
DAP contested 11 seats in the recent state election, retaining nine but losing Chennah and Repah. — Bernama

Title: Budget screening nears completion, Economy Ministry to forward 2027 development proposals to MoF
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 10 — The Economy Ministry expects to complete its screening of development expenditure proposals for 2027 by the middle of this month, before submitting its recommendations to the Finance Ministry (MoF), Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said today.
He said the ministry is currently in the final stage of Budget screening as part of preparations for the Second Rolling Plan (RP2) under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP).
“At the Economy Ministry, we have reached the final stage of Budget screening before we submit the proposals we have drawn up for development expenditure in 2027 to MoF.
“I expect that by the middle of this month, all processes at the Economy Ministry will be completed,” he told reporters today after launching the STEM talent pilot programme at Penang Tech Dome here.
Akmal said the Budget preparation process goes through several stages, including submissions from the respective implementing ministries.
Development expenditure proposals are subsequently submitted to the Economy Ministry for coordination and recommendation under RP2 for next year, he added.
He said the ministry is considering new allocations that need to be recommended while also reviewing the requirements of ongoing projects.
Asked about the main priorities for the upcoming Budget, Akmal said the government must ensure that the programmes and objectives outlined under the 13MP are supported by sufficient implementation capacity.
He said some of the initiatives had already been approved under the First Rolling Plan (RP1), while further requirements would be considered under RP2.
“For RP2, there are certainly several areas where I see a need, whether in terms of infrastructure or how government development expenditure can enhance or accelerate our move towards the high-growth, high-value industries that we have proposed,” he said.
Akmal said the government would also continue to take into account current requirements involving infrastructure, facilities and the preparedness of its agencies.
He said development spending for 2027 would ultimately be geared towards strengthening the implementation of the 13MP.
“For development expenditure in 2027, we are looking at strengthening the 13th Malaysia Plan,” he said.

Title: Two boys reported missing last night found drowned at Pasir Gudang dam after overnight search
Article:
PASIR GUDANG, Aug 10 — The bodies of two primary schoolboys, who had been reported missing since last night, were recovered at a dam here by Fire and Rescue Department personnel early this morning.
The victims have been identified as Mohammad Haikal Ramzi, 12, and Muhd Adam Farish Arman, 11.
The two friends were believed to have drowned while playing at a dam in Jalan Murai 2 in Taman Scientex here yesterday evening.
“We were told the two children were earlier reported missing and their families became concerned when they did not return to their respective homes.
“Both victims were believed to have gone swimming in the dam based on the discovery of a bicycle and slippers belonging to one of the victims at the scene,” he said.
Pasir Gudang fire and rescue station operations commander Haizrul Rahmad said a water rescue team recovered Mohammad Haikal’s body at a depth of two metres and a distance of three metres from the dam’s edge at 2.12am.
He said Adam’s body was later found at a depth of two metres and a distance of 4.5 metres from the dam’s edge at 2.33am.
“The bodies of both victims were later handed over to the police for further action,” he said in a statement today.
Haizrul said the search and rescue operation, involving fire and rescue personnel from the Pasir Gudang and Skudai stations, ended at 3am.
He said a total of 19 personnel and six engines were earlier dispatched to the location at 11.49pm last night to conduct the search and rescue operation.

Title: Penang court acquits four men over iron rod attack on lawyer
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 10 — The Magistrate’s Court here today acquitted and discharged four men of a charge of abetting in the assault of a lawyer with an iron rod two years ago.
Magistrate Nadratun Naim Mohd Saidi made the ruling after finding that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against Koay Beng Ghee, 38, Teh Eng Tat, 38, Ng Weng Kooi, 43, and Yeoh Ee Seong, 48, at the close of the prosecution’s case.
The court also found inconsistencies in the prosecution’s case, resulting in a failure to establish the elements of the charge against Koay, Teh and Ng, who are marketing executives, and Yeoh, a businessman.
“The prosecution submitted 42 exhibits and called nine witnesses to testify. Having heard the testimony of the prosecution witnesses, examined the exhibits, conducted a maximum evaluation of the entire case and considered the submissions, the court finds that the prosecution has failed to establish a
prima facie
case.
“Therefore, the court orders all the accused to be discharged and acquitted of the charges without being called to enter their defence,” she said.
“Therefore, the court orders all the accused to be discharged and acquitted of the charges without being called to enter their defence,” he said.
On December 24, 2024, Koay, Teh and Ng were charged with abetting Yeoh in causing injury to Beh Hong Shien, 37, using an iron rod by the roadside at Persiaran Karpal Singh here at 9.50am on October 22, 2024.
Yeoh was subsequently charged on December 27, 2024, with abetting the other three accused in committing the same offence.
They were charged under Section 324 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 109 of the same Code, which provides for a maximum prison sentence of 10 years, a fine, whipping, or any two of these punishments upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor M. Darrshini prosecuted the case, while lawyer Muhamad Asri Abdul Hamid represented Koay, Teh and Ng, and lawyers Datuk Suhaimi Ibrahim, Mohd Khairul Fairuz and Marcia Geraldine Lopez represented Yeoh. — Bernama

Title: Cashless for all: E-wallets now a national habit for Malaysians across generations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — E-wallets were long seen as a young person’s habit — something for students splitting bills or twenty-somethings ordering food delivery. New data from Ipsos Malaysia’s E-Wallet Landscape 2026 report suggests that story is out of date.
According to the survey of 1,029 Malaysians aged 18-74, conducted in April 2026, the fastest-growing group of e-wallet users last year was not the young.
It was Malaysians aged 35-44, whose usage jumped nine percentage points to 64 per cent, and those 45 and above, up four points to 44 per cent. By contrast, the 25-34 age bracket — traditionally assumed to be the core e-wallet demographic — stayed flat at 65 per cent, while 18-24 year-olds crept up just two points to 64 per cent.
Four years ago, e-wallets skewed heavily young. Today, usage across every adult age band sits within roughly 20 percentage points of each other, with the middle-aged group essentially level with Gen Z and millennials.
Ipsos points to where Malaysians are actually using their wallets as a clue. The strongest growth in usage occasions is not in online shopping — it is in everyday, offline spending: food and beverage outlets, toll and parking payments, and retail purchases.
“Malaysia has moved beyond digital payment adoption to digital payment dependence. For
businesses, being part of consumers' preferred payment ecosystem is increasingly critical to staying relevant,” Ipsos said in its report.
These are precisely the transactions a working, car-owning, family-supporting 40-something does daily — grabbing lunch, paying for parking at the office, buying groceries. As e-wallets embedded themselves into these routine errands, they stopped being a “digital-native” tool and became simply how bills get paid.
The report’s authors describe this directly: e-wallets are “no longer just a younger generation’s payment tool,” but an “everyday habit embraced by Malaysians across different life stages.”
What this means for consumers
For those in their 40s, 50s, or 60s who may still associate e-wallets with their children’s or grandchildren’s spending habits, the data suggests you have plenty of company adopting the technology — and there are practical reasons to keep up:
Convenience is now table stakes at toll booths and parking. With cashless lanes expanding, an e-wallet can shave real time off a commute.
Trust concerns are being addressed. Among the two leading platforms — Touch ‘n Go eWallet and MAE — safety and reliability scores sit at 77-82 per cent, suggesting the platforms have matured well past their early, glitch-prone days.
Wide acceptance removes the old excuse. Both leading wallets now report 76-81 per cent perceived acceptance among users, meaning “not enough places take it” is no longer the compelling argument it used to be.
A word of caution
Wider adoption among older Malaysians also raises the stakes on digital literacy and scam awareness.
As this demographic — often with larger account balances and less exposure to phishing tactics targeting younger digital natives — moves more of its daily spending onto phone-based apps, financial institutions and regulators may need to sharpen consumer education aimed specifically at midlife and older users, not just the young.
The bigger picture, though, is one of normalisation. What began as a convenience for the tech-savvy has become closer to a national habit, according to Ipsos, cutting across income groups, professions, and now, age.

Title: Transboundary haze worsens as nine Sarawak areas record unhealthy air quality
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 10 — The number of areas in Sarawak recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings due to transboundary haze rose to nine this morning.
Based on the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), the areas were Kuching (161), Samarahan (161), Serian (179), Sri Aman (155), Sarikei (155), Sibu (158), Mukah (156), Bintulu (142) and Samalaju (141).
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are hazardous.
API data is updated hourly based on readings from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide. — Bernama
